questions.question: What is the stop deadline, in ms: the longest time from the coprocessor ceasing to feed the RP2350 watchdog (frozen while the panel keeps beating) to every output and power gate the coprocessor drives being at its reset state?
questions.why: R1 checks the watchdog timeout against this deadline (Research.md R1 row; IOBoard.md:221), and neither page states it; hardware/STATUS.md:32 gives no timeout. The monostable's 200 ms deadline does not cover a frozen coprocessor beside a beating panel (IOBoard.md:163; docs/Safety.md:51). The timeout must also exceed the longest legitimate stall, at least the 400 ms packaged-part sector-erase maximum. A deadline below that leaves no valid timeout while the output binding stays in the in-package flash.

questions.question: What is the longest legitimate stall of the coprocessor's main loop, in ms, that the watchdog timeout must exceed? Is it the 400 ms packaged-part maximum of one 4 kB sector erase alone, or longer, to cover a USB console write that blocks while the host does not read (up to 500 ms a write at pico-sdk 2.3.1's default) and a pass that holds both?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:221 and the R1 row take the sector erase as the longest stall. firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1096-1098 says a console print blocks for as long as the USB host takes. pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb.c waits up to PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, 500,000 us by default (stdio_usb.h:31-33, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/pico-sdk/2.3.1/src/rp2_common/pico_stdio_usb/include/pico/stdio_usb.h, read 2026-09-28T10:32:09Z), and the image does not override it. P2 cannot check the timeout's lower bound without this figure.
questions.for_quantity: Longest legitimate stall the watchdog timeout exceeds

questions.question: What clock error between an ESC and the bench, in percent, must the bidirectional DShot decoder accept? The tree states 'a percent or two' with no source, and the decoder is host-tested at ±5 % (4.75 and 5.25 samples a bit).
questions.why: R1 states the crystal's tolerance against the DShot decoder (IOBoard.md:111). The margin the decoder leaves for the RP2354B's clock is the ±5 % tested less the ESC's own error. That error has no source in the tree (docs/DShot.md:224).
questions.for_quantity: ESC clock offset from the bench

questions.question: What watchdog timeout, in ms, does the coprocessor image set?
questions.why: The R1 row asks R1 to check the watchdog timeout against the stop deadline and the longest legitimate stall. IOBoard.md:221 and hardware/STATUS.md:32 say the timeout is not stated, and the image enables no watchdog. Without a value, P2 can report only the window between the two bounds, not check a timeout.

questions.question: What total frequency error, in ppm, may the RP2354B's 12 MHz crystal have: tolerance at 25 °C plus stability over the operating temperature range, plus first-year aging if counted?
questions.why: Neither page states a tolerance the crystal must meet, and R1 is asked to state it against the DShot decoder and the CAN bit rate (IOBoard.md:111). The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, Table 597, read 2026-09-28T10:22:26Z) recommends the Abracon ABM8-272-T3 at ±30 ppm tolerance, ±30 ppm stability and ±5 ppm first-year aging. Its section 8.1.2.3 keeps design margin for a reference within 1,000 ppm. P2 cannot keep or drop a crystal on tolerance without a limit.

questions.question: What load capacitance in pF, highest ESR in Ohm and lowest drive-level rating in uW must the 12 MHz crystal meet?
questions.why: Neither page states them. The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, section 8.2.1.1, Table 597, read 2026-09-28T10:22:26Z) gives the ABM8-272-T3 a load capacitance of 10 pF, an ESR of at most 50 Ohm, a C0 of at most 3.0 pF and a drive level of 10 uW typical and 200 uW maximum. It says any change to the crystal parameters risks instability, and that the oscillator circuit is tuned for 3.3 V IOVDD. P2 cannot qualify another crystal without these values.
questions.for_quantity: 12 MHz crystal load capacitance, ESR and drive level

questions.question: Over what ambient temperature range, in °C, must the R1 parts be rated and the crystal stay within its tolerance: the 0 to 50 °C over which pull request #167 specifies the monostable window, or another range?
questions.why: Neither page states the IO board's operating temperature range. IOBoard.md:220 lists behaviour outside 0 to 50 °C as not analysed, and only for the interlock. Crystal stability, inductor saturation current and protection ratings are all specified over a temperature range. The RP2350 itself is rated -40 to 85 °C ambient (Table 1435).

questions.question: What inductance in uH (with its tolerance in %), lowest saturation current in A and highest DC resistance in mOhm must the RP2354B's core regulator inductor meet?
questions.why: Neither page states them (IOBoard.md:110). The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, section 6.3.8.2, read 2026-09-28T10:22:26Z) gives 3.3 uH ±20 %, at least 1.5 A and at most 250 mOhm, fully shielded and marked for polarity, and recommends the AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T. Section 6.3.8.3 asks for low inductance roll-off. P2 cannot keep or drop an inductor candidate without the values.
questions.for_quantity: core regulator inductor inductance, saturation current and DC resistance

questions.question: What ESD immunity must the USB protection give the USB port's lines, as IEC 61000-4-2 contact and air discharge voltages in kV?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:118 and :536 put the USB port's protection in R1 and state no level. The RP2350's own ratings, 2 kV HBM and 500 V CDM (Table 1434), are component-handling figures, not a system level. P2 cannot qualify a protection part without the level.

questions.question: What highest VBUS voltage in V and current in A must the protection on the RP2354B's USB port carry? Is it a data port whose VBUS is only sensed, or also the USB-C charger input of F8 at up to 3 A and 5 V on the same connector, with its CC1 and CC2 pins?
questions.why: Three things are not stated: whether the charger's USB-C input is the RP2354B's USB port (IOBoard.md:370), whether the USB port powers the logic (IOBoard.md:384), and the connector type (IOBoard.md:140). They set which lines the protection clamps and the current its VBUS path carries.
questions.for_quantity: USB port VBUS voltage and current

questions.question: What highest capacitance per line, in pF, may the USB protection add on D+ and D-?
questions.why: The RP2354B's port is a full-speed device, 12 Mb/s, with a 27 Ohm series resistor on each data line (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 12.7 and Table 1431). A clamp's capacitance loads those lines. Neither page states a limit, so P2 cannot drop a clamp on capacitance.

questions.question: What highest voltage, in V, may the USB protection let reach USB_DP and USB_DM (QFN-80 pins 67 and 66)? Give the clamping voltage at the ESD level asked in the ESD question, and the highest steady voltage those pins may see.
questions.why: The RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) types USB_DP and USB_DM as USB IO on USB_OTP_VDD (Tables 1426 and 1431). Its absolute maximum ratings (Table 1433) give a Voltage at IO for Standard and FT pins only. Table 1437 (USB IO) gives no input maximum. Neither page states a limit, so P2 cannot compare a clamp's clamping voltage with the rating of the pins it protects.
questions.for_quantity: highest voltage at USB_DP and USB_DM behind the USB protection

questions.question: Which connector type does the RP2354B's USB port use: USB Type-C or another type the owner names? How many lines must the protection cover: VBUS, D+ and D-, plus CC1 and CC2 on USB Type-C?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:140 says the USB connector type is not stated and leaves connectors to round 2, while IOBoard.md:118 and :536 put the port's protection in round 1 (R1). P1's VBUS question settles only whether the port shares the charger's USB-C connector (IOBoard.md:370). If it does not, the connector and so the lines to clamp stay open. A Type-C receptacle adds CC1 and CC2 to the lines. P2 cannot choose a protection array's channel count or voltage rating per line without it.
questions.for_quantity: USB connector type and number of protected lines

questions.question: Must the core regulator inductor be fully shielded and marked for polarity (yes or no for each), as section 6.3.8.2 of the RP2350 datasheet requires?
questions.why: Section 6.3.8.2 (build 2025-07-29, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) says 'L must be fully shielded' and 'The inductor must be marked for polarity'. Section 6.3.8.3 says field orientation affects the regulator's control loop and output voltage. P1's inductor question asks inductance, saturation current and DC resistance only. IOBoard.md:110 states neither shielding nor polarity marking, so P2 would keep an unmarked or unshielded inductor that meets the three figures.
questions.for_quantity: core regulator inductor shielding and polarity marking

questions.question: What highest shunt capacitance C0, in pF, and which cut and mode (fundamental AT-cut or another) must the 12 MHz crystal meet?
questions.why: Table 597 of the RP2350 datasheet (build 2025-07-29, read 2026-09-28T10:38:05Z) gives the ABM8-272-T3 a C0 of at most 3.0 pF and Fundamental-AT operation. Section 8.2.1.1 says 'Any changes to crystal parameters risk instability'. P1's crystal question asks load capacitance, ESR and drive level only. IOBoard.md:110 states neither C0 nor the mode, so P2 cannot drop a crystal on them.
questions.for_quantity: 12 MHz crystal shunt capacitance C0 and mode

questions.question: At most how many CAN frames does the panel send to the IO board during one flash stall of the RP2354B, within 400 ms (the W25Q16JV packaged sector-erase maximum) and within 3 ms (the packaged page-program maximum), in frames? From the tree: one request is outstanding at a time (shared/link/include/link_host.h:5-7), with a 1000 ms timeout (link_host.h:29). A read request is 1 frame and a 32-register write is 8 frames (shared/link/include/link_can.h:69-72). Polls come every 50 ms in runs of back-to-back transactions (firmware/iomcu/src/out_store.h:103-104). No count per stall is stated.
questions.why: R2 reports each controller's held frames against the frames the panel sends in a stall (Research.md:280, IOBoard.md:171). Without the count, the Q8 report has nothing to compare against.
questions.for_quantity: frames the panel sends during the flash stall
questions.asks: frames the panel sends during the flash stall

questions.question: At most how many CAN frames arrive at the IO board on the external CAN port during one flash stall, within 400 ms and within 3 ms, in frames?
questions.why: R2 reports for each controller the received frames it holds against the frames that arrive in a stall (Research.md:280). The row counts only the panel's frames on the link. Neither page counts the external port's traffic.
questions.for_quantity: frames arriving on the external CAN port during the flash stall

questions.question: Is the external CAN port's transceiver held in standby by the enable node while the enable node is low (yes or no)? The R2 row, IOBoard.md:57 and IOBoard.md:238 state it with no source. The owner decision of 2026-09-25 names the port and its own controller only. F13 puts only the 20 output ports and the UART socket behind the gate.
questions.why: It decides whether the external transceiver needs a standby input driven from the enable node. A yes excludes transceivers without one and brings that input under the powered-off isolation rule (IOBoard.md:192).
questions.for_quantity: external CAN transceiver standby while the enable node is low

questions.question: Within what time after the enable node falls must the external CAN transceiver be in standby, in ms? The pages give the output buffer under 1 µs and a power switch 5 ms (IOBoard.md:187-188, Monostable.md:112-113 at 23c82ca). They give no time for the transceiver.
questions.why: P2 cannot check a candidate's normal-to-standby mode-change time without a limit.
questions.for_quantity: time from the enable node falling to the external CAN transceiver in standby

questions.question: Does the external CAN port carry CAN FD frames, or classic CAN only (CAN FD or classic)?
questions.why: A classic-only controller, the MCP2515 seed among them, cannot take part on a CAN FD bus. The link's 'classic CAN without FD' (IOBoard.md:167) covers the display link only.

questions.question: What is the highest bit rate on the external CAN port, in kbit/s: the nominal rate, and for CAN FD the data-phase rate?
questions.why: The transceiver's rated data rate and loop delay, and the controller's clock and bit timing, are checked against it. The link's 1 Mbit/s (IOBoard.md:167) is for the display link only.
questions.for_quantity: external CAN port highest bit rate

questions.question: What is the longest total bus length on the external CAN port, in m?
questions.why: The transceiver's loop delay plus the cable's propagation delay must fit before the sample point at the port's bit rate. The limits of under 5 m and under 30 cm (IOBoard.md:177) are for the display link only.

questions.question: Is the external CAN port galvanically isolated from the IO board's ground, and for what working voltage, in V (0 V if not isolated)?
questions.why: An isolated port needs an isolated transceiver or an isolator, which changes every candidate. Neither page states what connects to the port or where its ground returns. The bench carries an ESC pack of up to 67.2 V (F15) and up to 150 A continuous on the onboard path (F2).
questions.for_quantity: external CAN port isolation working voltage

questions.question: What DC voltage must the external CAN transceiver's CANH and CANL pins withstand without damage (bus-fault rating), in V, apart from the round 2 connector protection? The highest voltage on the bench is the ESC pack's 67.2 V (F15).
questions.why: The seed transceivers differ in bus-fault rating, and neither page states one. Round 2 protection (IOBoard.md:536) is selected after R2 and does not set the transceiver's own rating.

questions.question: What DC voltage must the link CAN transceiver's CANH and CANL pins withstand without damage (bus-fault rating), in V? The link cable carries the display's 5 V supply beside CANH and CANL (F6, IOBoard.md:177).
questions.why: P2 cannot keep or drop a link transceiver on its bus-fault rating without a limit, and neither page states one.

questions.question: What is the largest frequency error the link CAN controller's clock may have, including temperature and ageing, in ppm? The tree requires the bit rate to come out exact (shared/can/include/can_timing.h:17-21) and says two nodes that disagree by 1 % fail on long frames. It states no limit.
questions.why: R2 states each controller's clock tolerance (Research.md:280, IOBoard.md:111). P2 cannot pass or fail a controller and its clock source without a limit.
questions.for_quantity: link CAN controller clock tolerance limit

questions.question: What is the largest frequency error the external CAN controller's clock may have, including temperature and ageing, in ppm?
questions.why: R2 states each controller's clock tolerance (Research.md:280). The external port's bit timing is not stated, and the link's figures do not carry over. P2 cannot pass or fail a controller without a limit.
questions.for_quantity: external CAN controller clock tolerance limit

questions.question: The IO board also powers the display through the link cable. Within what time after power is applied to the IO board must its link CAN controller acknowledge frames on the link, in ms?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:210 says this time is not measured, that it runs against the display's 1200 ms start-up self-test (docs/Bringup.md:43-45; firmware/panel/main/main.c:196 and :1079), and that no question asks it. A frame nobody acknowledges raises the panel's transmit error counter. At 128 the self-test reports the coprocessor off the bus (docs/Bringup.md:88-90; firmware/panel/main/selftest.c:88-100). Without a limit, P2 cannot check a controller's oscillator start-up and configuration time or a transceiver's power-up time.
questions.for_quantity: time from power-up to the link CAN controller acknowledging frames

questions.question: Does the hardware latch of F11 power up set, holding the gates disabled until the operator clears it, or clear, letting the gates follow the enable node once edges arrive? STATUS.md:340 holds that every stop latches and nothing re-arms on its own. A latch that powers up set also holds the gates disabled through a clear-release pulse of a '123-type monostable (Q9).
questions.why: The latch's element and its reset wiring (preset or cleared by the reset supervisor, or set by the enable node's level) follow from the power-up state. P2 cannot qualify the latch without it.

questions.question: Where does the latch of F11 sit: between the enable node and the gates, so the enable node keeps the monostable's own timing and test steps 7 and 10 of pull request #167 still read it, or on the enable node itself, so the node stays low after the first expiry? The gates are the output buffer's enable, the servo rail gate, both ESC pack switches and the external CAN transceiver's standby.
questions.why: It fixes which nodes the latch drives and which of its inputs fall under the powered-off isolation rule, and so the latch's fan-out, drive and I_off. P2 cannot qualify the latch without it.
questions.asks: latch place relative to the enable node and the gates

questions.question: What is the operator clear control of the latch (F11), and where does it sit: a push button on the IO board, a control on the display panel, or a lead to a remote button? F11's answer names no part and no connector.
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the clear input's isolation, pull and debounce, or state what round 1 selects for the control, without the control and its place. A control on the panel passes through firmware.
questions.asks: operator clear control and where it sits

questions.question: May a relay contact, like the bench's relays across BOOT and RESET, or firmware on either board drive the latch's clear? Pull request #167 puts no processor, register or firmware in the path from GPIO6 to either gate. A clear driven that way re-enables the gates with no operator at the bench. Answer for a relay and for firmware.
questions.why: It decides whether the clear input takes only a manual contact or also a logic signal, which sets the clear circuit and its isolation. P2 cannot qualify the latch's clear path without it.
questions.asks: relay or firmware clear under the GPIO6 path rule

questions.question: Is the one high-side switch on the servo rail the servo rail's gate, and are the 20 port supply switches, which the I/O expander drives, not a gate? The Not defeatable rule of pull request #167 keeps a gate off the I/O expander.
questions.why: If the port switches were the gate, R3 selects no rail switch and the gate sits behind the I/O expander, against the Not defeatable rule. P2 cannot start the servo rail gate until this is confirmed.
questions.asks: port switches are not the servo rail gate

questions.question: What voltage margin, in V, above the 67.2 V of a 16-cell pack at 4.2 V a cell (F15) are the ESC pack switches rated for, on the onboard and the external path? An 80 V part leaves 12.8 V and a 100 V part 32.8 V. The INA238 on the pack node is rated to 85 V at most.
questions.why: It sets the drain-source rating of the MOSFET array, the voltage rating of its driver and of the external module, and the window between the pack voltage and the clamp. P2 cannot qualify any of them without it.

questions.question: What is the highest current, in A, on the external ESC pack path? The tree gives above 150 A to 300 A and more (owner, 2026-09-25).
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the external module's current rating, its safe operating area during turn-off, or the external path's protection without an upper figure.

questions.question: What drift of the monostable's timing constant k, in %, over 3.3 V ±3 % and 0 to 50 °C does the window budget take? Pull request #167 assumes ±3 % (k = 0.45 at 3.3 V and 25 °C), and the window's margin of 2.7 ms each way rests on it. Give a figure, or mark it for research: read from the candidate's datasheet, where parts of this class graph k and state no limit.
questions.why: P2 cannot pass or fail a monostable against the 155 to 185 ms window at every corner without the k drift the budget takes.
questions.for_quantity: monostable k drift over supply and temperature

questions.question: What timing-pin leakage, in µA at 50 °C, does the window budget take? Pull request #167 assumes 0.5 µA, against the class's 1 µA limit at 85 °C, and books ±2 % of window drift for it. Give a figure, or mark it for research: the candidate's 25 °C figure, doubled every 10 °C.
questions.why: The leakage term is 2 of the 7.25 % drift budget. P2 cannot pass or fail a monostable on the window without it.

questions.question: What ambient temperature range, in °C, do the safety gate and the ESC pack switches work across? Pull request #167 assumes 0 to 50 °C for the bench, analyses the window only there, and leaves behaviour outside it open.
questions.why: The window's corners, each part's operating range and the switches' current derating use it. P2 cannot qualify a part's temperature range without it.

questions.question: What off-state leakage, in mA, may the open servo rail gate pass? Pull request #167 sets 5 mA per rail as a placeholder until a load's idle current is measured; a small servo idles at 5 to 10 mA, not measured.
questions.why: P2 cannot pass or fail a switch's off-state current without the limit.
questions.for_quantity: servo rail gate off-state leakage limit

questions.question: What off-state leakage, in mA, may an open ESC pack switch pass, on the onboard and the external path, any precharge path around it included? The specification applies the servo rail's 5 mA placeholder. The ESC in pull request #167's example idles at 50 mA.
questions.why: It qualifies the MOSFETs' and the external module's off-state current, and decides whether a precharge resistor may stay across an open switch.
questions.for_quantity: ESC pack switch off-state leakage limit

questions.question: What highest sustained input voltage, in V, does the ESC pack path's overvoltage protection survive while it keeps the pack node under 85 V, for example a pack of more than 16 cells connected by mistake? Answer none if only switching transients are clamped. Only the research plan states this protection; no owner answer does.
questions.why: P2 cannot choose between a clamp and a series disconnect, or rate its MOSFETs, without the sustained voltage it survives.

questions.question: What largest ESC input capacitance, in µF, does the ESC pack switch precharge before it closes fully? Answer none if no precharge is required. Pull request #167 gives one example ESC with 470 µF. Only the research plan states the precharge; no owner answer does.
questions.why: P2 cannot size the precharge, or the MOSFETs' safe operating area while closing, without the capacitance.

questions.question: What shortest delay, in ms, does the reset supervisor hold the clear after the 3.3 V rail passes its threshold? The 3.3 V ramp time is not stated, and R5 selects the regulator after T2.
questions.why: P2 cannot pick or pass a supervisor's delay option without a minimum. P5 later checks it against R5's ramp.

questions.question: What highest voltage, in V, is the servo rail gate rated for? The rail is set to 8.4 V at most, and the TPS55285 can be programmed to 15 V over I²C.
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the gate's voltage rating without it. A fault that programs the converter above 8.4 V reaches the gate before the port ceilings of F16.

questions.question: What inductance, in µH, do the pack leads to the IO board and to the external module have, for the transient the clamp absorbs when a switch opens at full current (energy = 0.5 x L x I², at 150 A onboard)? A TVS diode rated 70 V working (Vishay SMBJ70A) breaks down at 77.8 to 86.0 V and clamps at 113 V at 5.3 A.
questions.why: P2 cannot size the clamp's energy or the MOSFETs' safe operating area during turn-off without the transient; IOBoard.md:385 states the transient level is not given.

questions.question: What longest time, in ms, may an ESC pack switch take to close, precharge included, from the enable rising or the latch clearing?
questions.why: P2 cannot size the precharge resistor, its power, or an inrush slew rate without a closing-time limit.

questions.question: Does the closed ESC pack switch carry current from the ESC back into the pack, as in regenerative braking, and up to what current in A? A reverse-polarity stage built as an ideal diode blocks it. The BENCH current register sends a negative current as 0 A.
questions.why: It decides whether the driver may be an ideal-diode controller and what reverse current the array carries. P2 cannot qualify the driver or the array's arrangement without it.

questions.question: What highest current, in A, does each ESC pack switch open without damage: the motor overcurrent trip level plus its rise during detection, or a short-circuit figure? The switch opens on the enable falling and on the coprocessor's overcurrent action.
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the MOSFETs' or the external module's safe operating area during turn-off without the current they interrupt.

questions.question: What highest dissipation, in W, may the onboard ESC pack switch have at 150 A continuous? It sets how many MOSFETs share the current. The onboard shunt beside it dissipates 2.25 W at 100 µΩ and 4.5 W at 200 µΩ.
questions.why: Sourcing rule 4 needs the placements range and its basis; P2 cannot size the array's on-resistance and count without a dissipation limit.

questions.question: Is the external path's highest current continuous, or a peak, and if a peak, for how long in s?
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the external module's current rating and its temperature rise at that current without the duty.

questions.question: What lowest ESC pack voltage, in V, does each ESC pack switch close and conduct at? SET_PACK_CELLS takes 1 cell (shared/settings/settings.c:39-41), and no per-cell floor is stated for the ESC pack.
questions.why: P2 cannot qualify the driver's supply range or the MOSFETs' gate drive at the lowest pack voltage without it.

questions.question: Does the latch of F11 set on the enable node's low level, or on its falling edge? With a level set, a clear given while the enable is low leaves the gates disabled, and so does a clear control held or stuck closed. With an edge set, a clear given while the panel is stopped lets the gates return when the edges resume, with no operator action at that moment. Answer level or falling edge, and say which input wins when set and clear are both active.
questions.why: The answer fixes the latch element: a set-dominant latch fed by the level, or an edge-triggered flip-flop with a clear. It also fixes whether its set overrides its clear. STATUS.md:340 holds that nothing re-arms on its own. P2 cannot qualify the latch without it. Question 0 asks the power-up state only.

questions.question: How does the coprocessor's overcurrent and over-temperature action open the ESC pack switches? The options are an RP2354B output on a second, disable-only input of each switch driver, or no switch action at all: the throttle stops, and the switches follow the enable node alone. IOBoard.md:475 and the R8 row time the path 'from detection to the ESC pack switch open'. The R3 row says R3's gates follow the enable node alone. IOBoard.md:197 puts no processor in the path from GPIO6 to a gate.
questions.why: A second input changes the driver's logic to an AND of the enable node and an RP2354B output. It adds an input under the powered-off isolation rule, and its level during an RP2354B reset decides whether the pack switches open through that reset, which the R3 row says they do not. P2 cannot qualify the onboard driver or the external module's driver output without it. P5 cannot budget the motor overcurrent path without it.

questions.question: What inductance, in µH, do the leads between each ESC pack switch and the ESC have? When a high-side switch opens at full current, that inductance keeps the current flowing into the ESC's input capacitance. That drives the switched node negative until a clamp conducts. The energy is 0.5 x L x I²: 11 mJ at 1 µH and 150 A. The INA238 takes -0.3 V at least on VBUS, IN+ and IN- (SLYS025B section 5.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina238.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:40:16Z).
questions.why: Question 18 covers only the pack-side leads, which set the positive transient. Without the switched side's inductance, P2 cannot size the clamp on the switched node or the MOSFETs' avalanche energy during turn-off. P5 cannot check the INA238 where it sits on the switched side; the shunt's side is not stated (IOBoard.md:469).

questions.question: What lowest servo rail voltage, in V, does the servo rail gate close and conduct at? The rail has two settings, up to 5.5 V and up to 8.4 V, set from software (hardware/STATUS.md:37). The TPS55285 programs 0.8 V to 15 V (SLVSI72A, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:40:16Z).
questions.why: A high-side switch has a lowest supply at which its driver turns it fully on. P2 cannot pass or fail the gate's supply range, or a P-channel gate's drive, without the lowest rail voltage.

questions.question: What selects the pull-up or pull-down of F14 on each of the 4 multiprotocol ports: a jumper per port, an RP2354B GPIO, an output of the I/O expander that drives the port switches, or a circuit with no control input that follows the port's signal?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:256 says what selects the bias is not stated, and R4 selects the part that sets it. P2 cannot choose the element or count its placements and control lines without the answer. The element could be a jumper, an analogue switch or MOSFET per port, or a buffer with its own pull.

questions.question: Does a bias selector driven by RP2354B firmware or by the I/O expander meet the rule that no processor, register or firmware sits in the path from GPIO6 to a gate (Monostable.md:449-455 at 23c82ca): yes or no? The selector is not in the enable path, but it sets the connector line's level while the gate is disabled.
questions.why: A selected pull-up holds a disabled line high. Pull request #167 makes low the disabled idle for servo pulses and DShot (Monostable.md:363-366). If the answer is no, the selector is a jumper or is driven from the enable node. P2 cannot qualify a firmware- or expander-driven selector until then.

questions.question: What high level must each port's signal line drive at the connector, in V: 3.3 V, 5 V, or the level of a supply sensed from the device, and then which rail? It applies to the 16 PWM ports, the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket.

questions.question: Which wire does VESC's 115,200-baud framed-packet link use on the IO board, and how many signal lines does it take: one half-duplex line on a multiprotocol port, the UART socket, or separate transmit and receive lines (2)?

questions.question: What is the highest baud rate of any receiver bus on a receiver input, in baud? The buses are iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2 and JETI EX Bus; S.BUS is 100 kbaud.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:287 says the baud of iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2 and JETI EX Bus is not stated. P2 checks any input buffer or filter against the highest rate.

questions.question: Does the bench transmit on a receiver input, for JETI EX Bus telemetry (docs/Manifest.md:37-39) or SRXL2: yes or no, for each bus?

questions.question: Does a receiver input pass the output gate of F13: yes or no? F13's answer names only the 20 output ports and the UART socket.

questions.question: The gate stays enabled while the RP2354B is held in reset or restarts through the watchdog, because the enable follows the monostable (owner, 2026-09-25). questions.question: When an ESC or a servo has to start up with its signal line held high to enter its bootloader or CLI, what powers it up? questions.question: What is the lowest voltage, in V, the display takes at its end of the link cable while it draws 2 A?

questions.question: Does the display's own power path isolate the VBUS of each of its USB-C sockets from the 5 V it takes from the link cable: yes or no? questions.question: What is the highest voltage, in V, the display takes at its end of the link cable at no load?

questions.question: At which current, in A, does the link cable's supply limit a short on the cable so that the IO board's own rails stay up? Answer 'none' if it has no limit.
questions.why: The answer decides between an ideal diode, which has no limit, and an eFuse, which limits current. The busfault screen names a connector only nearly seated as a known fault. No requirement states a limit.

questions.question: What is the highest continuous voltage, in V, the DC input survives without damage? Examples: a 24 V supply, or a 6S pack at 25.2 V, connected by mistake.
questions.why: It sets the absolute maximum rating P2 qualifies the input protection against. The pages give only the 12 to 20 V operating range. The TPS25947 seed is rated 28 V continuous.

questions.question: At which DC input voltage, in V, does the overvoltage protection cut the input off? It lies above the 20 V maximum and at or below the TPS55285's 22 V input rating. Does 20 V include the DC source's own tolerance?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:332 and :374 state that the threshold is not stated. P2 cannot check a protector's trip point or its tolerance band without it.

questions.question: What transient does the DC input's protection absorb: its peak in V and its duration in µs? An example is the ringing of a lead hot-plugged onto ceramic input capacitors.
questions.why: Without a transient level, P2 cannot size a TVS (transient-voltage-suppression) clamp or check a protector's transient rating. The pages name no transient for the board input; R3 covers transients only on the ESC pack path.

questions.question: Do the reverse-polarity, overvoltage and inrush protection sit on the 2S pack input as well as on the 12 to 20 V DC input: yes or no?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:331-333 place each one 'on the board's power input', and the board has two inputs. P2 qualifies a protection part for the pack input only if the answer is yes.

questions.question: What is the highest inrush current, in A, the board may draw when the DC input or the 2S pack is connected?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:333 and :374 state that the limit is not stated. P2 cannot set or check a soft-start or current-limit part without it.

questions.why: IOBoard.md:374 lists the lowest input voltage the board runs from as not known. Without it, P2 cannot set the selection's switchover threshold or the DC input's undervoltage lockout.

questions.question: What is the longest interruption, in ms, the 3.3 V rail and the 5 V rail with the display may see when the DC input is connected or removed while the board runs? Answer 0 for none.
questions.why: A drop at the display stops the heartbeat and opens every gate (docs/Safety.md:24-30). A drop on the 3.3 V rail resets the RP2354B. P2 cannot choose between diode-OR selection, a priority switch with hold-up capacitance and a make-before-break controller without this figure.

questions.question: Which pack path current, in A, does R5 size the source selection and the pack disconnect for? questions.question: Does the RP2354B's USB port power the board's logic when neither the DC input nor the pack is present: yes or no? If yes, which rails: the 3.3 V rail only, or also the 5 V rail and the display?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:384 states it is not known. A yes adds a third source, with its own current limit, to the selection P2 qualifies.

questions.question: What reconnects the pack after a floor disconnect: the USB-C charger present, the DC input present, every cell above a stated voltage, or an operator action? Name one or more.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:330 states that the condition is not stated, and F9's answer sets the floor only. The condition decides whether P2 needs a voltage comparator with hysteresis, a latch, or a charger-present input.

questions.question: Is 3.0 V the lowest cell voltage at which the disconnect trips at every tolerance corner, or its nominal trip point? What tolerance, in mV, does the trip point hold over 0 to 50 °C?
questions.why: Without it, P2 cannot check a protector's undervoltage threshold accuracy, or pick a factory-trim or resistor-set threshold.

questions.why: The pack sources up to about 9.9 A. Without a delay, a servo current step can sag a cell below 3.0 V and disconnect the pack. P2 cannot check a protector's undervoltage delay without this figure.

questions.question: What is the highest current, in µA, the board may draw from the pack while the pack is disconnected?
questions.why: The circuit that holds a pack at 3.0 V a cell off keeps drawing from it. P2 cannot rank monitors and protectors by their quiescent current without a limit.

questions.question: Which of these may the pack's floor disconnect be: (a) a part of its own, with the 3.0 V threshold fixed by resistors or factory trim; (b) the pack protection R7 selects; (c) a protector whose threshold firmware writes over I²C at start-up?
questions.why: 'In hardware' (owner, 2026-09-24) does not settle (b) or (c). R5 and R7 run side by side in T3, and the answer decides whether R5 selects a disconnect part at all.

questions.question: What current margin, in %, do the 3.3 V logic buck and the 5 V rail each hold above their load? The load is summed from the parts T2 and T4 select and the display. The margin covers the parts R6, R7 and R8 select in the same task.

questions.question: Which tolerance, in %, does the 5 V rail hold at the IO board's own 5 V loads: the load-cell excitation (F3) and the encoder's 5 V supply (F4)?
questions.why: No accuracy is stated for the 5 V rail. P2 cannot check the regulator's setpoint accuracy, load regulation and ripple without it.

questions.question: What is the lowest bridge resistance, in Ω, of the load cells on the 3 channels (F3)?
questions.why: The bridge resistance sets the excitation current on the 5 V rail: 5 V divided by it, for each cell. IOBoard.md:338 states that the excitation current is not stated. The load cells are sensors, not parts T4 selects.

questions.question: What is the highest supply current, in mA, of the encoder at 12 V and at 5 V (F4)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:387 states that the encoder's current is not stated. The encoder is the operator's device, not a part T2 or T4 selects. P2 cannot size the 12 V buck-boost or the encoder's share of the 5 V rail without it.

questions.question: Which voltage range, in V, does the encoder's 12 V supply hold at the encoder's connector?
questions.why: F4 gives 12 V with no tolerance. P2 cannot check the buck-boost's output accuracy across the 6.0 to 20 V input without it.

questions.question: Does the IO board power the receiver: yes or no? If yes, from which rail, at which voltage in V, and at which highest current in mA?
questions.why: The R5 row includes the receiver's supply only if the board powers one. IOBoard.md:287 and docs/Receivers.md:15-16 name signal and ground only, and docs/Receivers.md:29 names receiver power as a cause of a silent bus. P2 cannot qualify a supply or switch for it without the answer.

questions.question: Which DC input current, in A, does R5 size the DC input's protection and the source selection for? Option 1: 4.9 A for the servo supply at 12 V, on the 90 % efficiency Power.md:68 assumes, plus the display, the encoder's 12 V supply and the logic rails. Option 2: the TPS55285's input current from its datasheet efficiency at 12 V in and 8.4 V, 6.35 A out ('for research'), plus the same loads.

The display adds 7.5 W / 0.9 / 12 V = 0.69 A, making 5.63 A before the logic rails. That is above the TPS25947 seed's 5.5 A rating (www.ti.com/product/TPS25947, read 2026-09-28T10:33:19Z). questions.question: In which order do the IO board's 5 V and 3.3 V rails come up at power-on and fall at power-off: 5 V first, 3.3 V first, or either order?

questions.question: With the 2S pack's power leads connected and its balance lead unplugged, or one balance wire open, does the disconnect hold the pack off: yes or no?

P2 cannot check whether a monitor detects an open balance wire, or whether the pack path defaults off, without the answer.

questions.question: At which current, in mA, is the encoder's supply output (5 V or 12 V, F4) limited, so that a short on the encoder cable leaves the 5 V rail and the display's supply in regulation? Answer 'none' if it has no limit.

questions.question: What output current must the servo rail deliver at the 5.5 V setting and at the 8.4 V setting, in A? What current limit applies at each setting, in A?

questions.question: What current must the servo rail deliver at the 8.4 V setting while the converter runs from the pack, with 6.0 to 8.4 V at its input, in A?

questions.for_quantity: Rail current required at 8.4 V from the pack

questions.question: What efficiency do the servo converter's pack figures use from 6.0 to 8.4 V in at 8.4 V out, in %: 90 %, or the figure R6 reads from the TPS55285 datasheet (for research)?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:326 borrows 90 % from Power.md's DC-input figure. The datasheet gives no efficiency at 6.0 V in. P2 computes the inductor's DC current at the low end as VOUT x IOUT / (VIN x efficiency).
questions.for_quantity: Servo converter efficiency from the pack

questions.question: What is the highest voltage the DC input can present at the servo converter's VIN, in V, as a steady value and as a transient with its duration in ms?
questions.why: The DC input is 12 to 20 V with no tolerance, and R5's overvoltage threshold is not stated (IOBoard.md:374). The TPS55285 is specified to 22 V. questions.question: What is the lowest voltage at the servo converter's VIN when it runs from the pack, in V? Is it 6.0 V, or 6.0 V less a stated drop across the pack path (R5's disconnect, source selection and protection) at the pack current?

questions.question: What is the highest voltage allowed at a port's supply pin at each setting, in V? Are 5.5 V and 8.4 V upper limits that include setpoint tolerance, ripple and load-step overshoot, or nominal setpoints? If nominal, what tolerance applies, in V?

questions.question: What drives the servo converter's EN/UVLO pin: an RP2354B GPIO, an I/O expander output, or a divider from its input with the output switched only over I2C?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:340 requires the converter off while its driving pin is an input, and states that what drives it is not stated. The answer adds one expander output or one GPIO.

questions.question: What ambient temperature range must the IO board operate in, in C?
