questions.question: At which switching frequency does the servo converter run: 400 kHz, 800 kHz, 1.6 MHz or 2.1 MHz? Or is it marked for research?
questions.why: The inductance must exceed 1.2/fSW and sets the ripple (SLVSI72A 8.2.2.3). TI recommends 400 or 800 kHz at high current (6.3.7). The tree states none, so P2 cannot fix the inductance it qualifies.

questions.question: What current must the inductor's saturation rating exceed, in A: the peak current at the highest operating point, or the TPS55285's cycle-by-cycle peak current limit (13 A typical)?
questions.why: The datasheet requires saturation above the calculated peak (SLVSI72A 8.2.2.3). It gives the peak limit as 13 A typical with no minimum or maximum, and its example inductor saturates at 15.2 A. An overload drives the inductor to that limit. The choice sets the inductor's size class.

questions.question: How many outputs must the I/O expander drive? Is it the 20 port supply switches only, or also the servo converter's enable and R4's bias selectors?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:348 and 383 name the 20 port switches. IOBoard.md:340 leaves the converter's enable driver open, and IOBoard.md:256 asks whether R4's bias selector may sit on the I/O expander. P2 needs the count to qualify one expander or several.

questions.question: At what clock rate does the coprocessor's I2C bus that carries the I/O expander and the TPS55285 run, in kHz?
questions.why: The rate is not stated (IOBoard.md:481). The TPS55285 takes 100 to 1000 kHz (SLVSI72A 5.5). P2 checks the expander's rated clock against the bus rate.

questions.question: Are the 20 port supply switches not the servo rail gate, which is then R3's single high-side switch on the rail: yes or no?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:218 names R3 and R6 and asks for this confirmation; R3's P1 asks the same item. If the port switches were the gate, each would need I_off or 4.7 kOhm on its control input, 5 ms opening, failing open when undriven, and under 5 mA off (IOBoard.md:188, 192). None could then be driven through the I/O expander.

questions.question: What continuous current must each port's supply switch carry, in A?
questions.why: The rating is not stated (IOBoard.md:379). Firmware aborts one servo above 3.0 A and a synchronised pair above 4.0 A (docs/Servo.md:35, 68-69), and the rail gives 6.35 A at most. P2 qualifies each switch's current rating and on-resistance.

questions.question: Must each port supply switch limit its own current? If so, at what value, in A?
questions.why: The limit is not stated (IOBoard.md:536). The rail's only limit is the TPS55285's, up to 6.35 A, shared by 20 ports. A shorted port or a servo's inrush pulls the whole rail into limit. Parts with and without a current limit differ.

questions.question: What voltage drop is allowed from the servo rail to a port's supply pin at the port's rated current, in mV?
questions.why: Each port has its switch and a 10 mOhm monitor shunt in series (IOBoard.md:351), and no drop is stated. P2 checks each switch's on-resistance against the allowed drop.

questions.question: What off-state leakage may an open port supply switch pass at 8.4 V, in mA?
questions.why: Signal-only mode disconnects the supply pin (IOBoard.md:349). Only the servo rail gate has a leakage limit, a 5 mA placeholder (IOBoard.md:188). P2 checks each switch's off-state leakage against the answer.

questions.question: Must a port supply switch block current flowing from the port's supply pin back into the servo rail? If so, up to what voltage on the pin, in V?
questions.why: A port lead carries signal, ground and rail (IOBoard.md:531). An ESC's BEC drives a regulated voltage onto that rail wire to feed the receiver and servos (docs/OpenYGE.md:253). The tree states no requirement, and switches with and without reverse blocking differ.

questions.question: What is the longest time allowed from an RP2354B reset (watchdog, RUN or power loss) until every port supply switch is open, in ms?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:221 leaves open the stop deadline the watchdog serves; R1's P1 asks for it. Whatever remains after the watchdog timeout is R6's budget for the expander's reset path and the switch's turn-off with a servo's capacitance on the port. P2 qualifies turn-off time against it.

questions.question: What trip band is allowed for each ceiling, in V? For the LV and HV positions, what is the lowest voltage at which each may cut a port off, and the highest at which each must?
questions.why: F16 gives 6.0 V and 8.7 V with no tolerance. The 8.4 V setting at the converter's +/-1.5 % accuracy reaches 8.53 V before ripple and transients. P2 qualifies the ceiling part's threshold accuracy against the band.

questions.question: Within what time must a port be cut off once its supply pin exceeds its ceiling, in microseconds?
questions.why: F16's answer states no response time. P2 needs one to qualify an overvoltage detector or protected switch.

questions.question: After a ceiling cut-off, does the port reconnect by itself once the rail falls below the ceiling? If so, with what hysteresis, in V? Or does it stay off until an operator or firmware action?
questions.why: F16's answer states the cut-off only. Auto-retry and latch-off parts differ.

questions.question: What is the 2S pack's full-charge voltage, in V: 8.4 V (2 x 4.2 V), or the charge voltage of the cell and charger R7 selects?
questions.why: Research.md:284 checks the TPS55285 from the floor of F9 up to the pack's full charge. F9's answer gives the chemistry and the 3.0 V floor only. 4.2 V a cell entered IOBoard.md:325 in commit 8d8964f without a source. P2 checks the converter's input range against the top of this range, and its mode at the 8.4 V setting: buck-boost at 8.4 V in, buck above it.
questions.for_quantity: Pack voltage range at the converter's input

questions.question: What input current from the pack, in A, do the servo supply's inductor and the pack path take at the 6.0 V floor: 9.9 A (8.4 V x 6.35 A at an assumed 90 %), or the TPS55285's average inductor current limit, 7 A minimum and 8 A typical, with no maximum stated?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:326 computes 7.1 A and 9.9 A from an assumed 90 % and from 6.35 A at 8.4 V from the pack, which IOBoard.md:345 marks not checked. In boost mode the input current is the inductor current (SLVSI72A equation 7, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:37:06Z). The average inductor current limit clamps it (5.4). That limit has no maximum, and the only other bound is the peak limit, 13 A typical. R6 sizes the inductor's DC current from this figure, and R5 and R7 size the pack path and the cells.
questions.for_quantity: Servo supply input current from the pack

questions.question: What capacitance must a port supply switch charge at turn-on, in uF, and what peak inrush current may it draw from the servo rail while doing so, in A?
questions.why: The tree states no capacitance on a port's supply pin and no turn-on requirement (IOBoard.md:348, 379). The rail's only current limit is the TPS55285's: at most 6.35 A, with a 128 us default response (SLVSI72A 7.3, read 2026-09-28T10:37:06Z), shared by 20 ports. A port switched onto an uncharged capacitance pulls down the rail for the other 19. P2 chooses between switches with and without a controlled rise time from these figures.

questions.question: What is the highest current the servo rail may deliver into a shorted port, in A: 6.35 A, with firmware keeping the TPS55285's output current limit enabled and its response at 128 us, or the average inductor current limit the converter falls back to otherwise, 7 A minimum and 8 A typical, with no maximum stated?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:343 and Power.md:60 treat 6.35 A as a hard ceiling. SLVSI72A (read 2026-09-28T10:37:06Z) lets firmware clear Current_Limit_EN (7.2, register 02h bit 7). It also lets firmware delay the limit by up to 1.024 x 12 ms (OCP_DELAY, 7.3). A port switch with no limit of its own (IOBoard.md:536) carries this current until it opens. P2 qualifies each switch's current rating against the answer.

questions.question: Must the RP2354B read, for each of the 20 ports, whether the ceiling has cut the port off and which ceiling its jumper selects? Yes or no for each.
questions.why: F16's answer and IOBoard.md:350 give the cut-off and the jumper, and nothing that reaches firmware. The SETUP stub lists the ceilings only as set in hardware (shared/ui/stub_screen.c:56). A trip report needs a fault output on the ceiling part, and the two reports together take up to 40 inputs through the I/O expander or GPIO. P2 qualifies the ceiling part and sizes the expander from the answer.

questions.question: What is the highest voltage the port supply switches and the ceiling parts must withstand at their input, in V: 15 V (the TPS55285's recommended maximum output), 17 V (its VOUT absolute maximum), 20 V (the DC input through a failed converter), or about 21.3 V (the highest target its registers can set)?
questions.why: The ceiling cuts a port off above 6.0 V or 8.7 V (F16), so the ceiling part and the port switch see whatever the rail reaches. SLVSI72A (read 2026-09-28T10:37:06Z) recommends at most 15 V out (5.2) and gives VOUT an absolute maximum of 17 V (5.1). Its registers reach further. Table 7-6 gives 20 V at INTFB 11b and REF 0780h. REF reaches 1.2 V, which is 21.3 V at ratio 0.0564 (7.1, 7.4). Firmware can disable the output overvoltage protection (FB_OVP, 7.4). P2 checks each part's absolute maximum against the answer.

questions.question: How many 18650 cells does the bench's 2S pack hold: 2 (2S1P, each cell carrying the whole pack current), or more in parallel, for example 4 (2S2P)? Answer with the number of cells.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:359 and hardware/STATUS.md:25 state 2 cells, but their sources fix only the series count. The owner decision at Research.md:61 gives 2S, F9 the chemistry and the floor, and S9 the makers. P2 checks each cell's continuous-discharge rating against the whole pack current for 2S1P, about 11.3 A plus the logic rails at 6.0 V, and against half of it for 2S2P. The cell count also sets the placements per pack for the stock gate (rule 4).

questions.question: What charge voltage per cell, in V, does the charger regulate the pack to: 4.2 V (8.4 V for the pack), or the charge voltage in the selected cell's datasheet?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:325 takes 4.2 V a cell and cites F9. F9's Answer states only lithium-ion 18650 and a 3.0 V floor. 4.2 V is in F9's proposed answer, and a proposed answer is not an answer (Research.md:501). The BQ25887 is specified at 4.20 V and 4.35 V a cell (SLUSD89B). Without this value P2 cannot set the charger's regulation voltage or check it against the cell. R5 and R6 take 8.4 V as the pack's highest voltage.

questions.question: What charger efficiency, in %, does R7 take from 5 V at 3 A into the pack between 6.0 V and 8.4 V? Or is it for research, from the selected charger's datasheet?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:363 and Power.md:98 assume 90 % with no source. That figure gives the 13.5 W into the pack, 1.6 A at 8.4 V and 2.25 A at 6.0 V, against which P2 judges a 2 A charger. The BQ25887 datasheet gives one point only: 93.4 % at 5 V in, 7.6 V battery and 1 A charge.

questions.question: What efficiency, in %, does R7 take for the TPS55285 running from the pack at 6.0 V and delivering 8.4 V at 6.35 A? Or is it for research, from the TPS55285 datasheet?
questions.why: The R7 row takes 90 %, the figure Power.md:68 uses for the 12 to 20 V DC input. IOBoard.md:326 states that the efficiency from the pack is not stated. This value sets the 9.9 A at the 6.0 V floor, the largest part of the pack current. P2 checks the cell's continuous-discharge rating and sets the pack's overcurrent protection against that current.
questions.for_quantity: servo supply efficiency from the pack

questions.question: What efficiency, in %, does R7 take for the 5 V rail that feeds the display's 7.5 W (5 V x 1.5 A continuous) from the pack at 6.0 V? Or is it for research?
questions.why: The R7 row assumes 90 %, which gives about 1.4 A from the pack (repeated at IOBoard.md:359). The 5 V converter is R5's and is selected in the same task, T3, so R7's P2 has no verified figure. The result adds to the pack current the cell and the overcurrent protection are sized for.
questions.for_quantity: 5 V rail efficiency from the pack

questions.question: What balance current per cell, in mA, must the charger or a separate balancer provide?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:364 leaves the balance current not chosen. Its claim that 400 mA balances within one charge and 50 mA overnight (Power.md:109) rests on a cell imbalance in mAh that no source states. The answer decides between two routes: a charger with integrated balancing (BQ25887, up to 400 mA), or a split charger with a 15 to 50 mA balancer (BQ25798 with BQ29209 or BQ76907, Power.md:103-107).

questions.question: What current, in A drawn from the pack at 6.0 V, does R7 budget for the loads other than the servo supply and the display? These are the 3.3 V logic rail, the load-cell excitation and 5 V encoder supply on the 5 V rail, and the encoder's 12 V supply boosted from the pack.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:359 adds 'the logic rails, which are not stated' to the pack current. IOBoard.md:338 and :387 leave the excitation and encoder currents unstated. R5 sizes these rails in the same task, T3. R7's P2 therefore has no figure when it checks the cell's continuous-discharge rating and sets the overcurrent protection.
questions.for_quantity: logic rail current from the pack

questions.question: What is the lowest charge current into the pack, in A, that the charger must deliver from a USB-C source advertising 3.0 A?
questions.why: F8 (Research.md:536) sets a ceiling on the draw, up to 3 A at 5 V, and no floor. The R7 row asks for charging 'at the current of F8'. Power.md:78 and :99-101 state that no single die from an allowed maker charges 2S above 2 A and balances it. They also state that a 2 A charger uses the whole budget only above 6.75 V. Whether 2 A is enough decides between one charger with balancing and a split charger plus balancer.
questions.for_quantity: lowest charge current into the pack

questions.question: What is the lowest capacity per cell, in mAh, that the pack's 18650 cells need? Or what run time, in minutes, from a full pack at a stated load?
questions.why: Neither page states a capacity or a run time. 18650 cells from the allowed makers trade continuous-discharge rating against capacity. P2 therefore has no requirement by which to qualify or rank the cells that pass the current check.

questions.question: Over which ambient temperature range, in °C, must the pack charge, and over which range must it discharge?
questions.why: The R7 row has R7 check the cell's temperature limits, and IOBoard.md:359 records them. Neither page states the range to check them against. The interlock is specified over 0 to 50 °C (IOBoard.md:184). The BQ25887 suspends charging below 0 °C and above 60 °C, and reduces it below 10 °C and above 45 °C (SLUSD89B, JEITA thermistor comparator).

questions.question: Does the 2S pack carry an NTC thermistor for the charger's temperature input? If so, what is its resistance at 25 °C in kΩ, and its B value in K?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:365 states that whether the pack carries one is not stated. The BQ25887 reads a thermistor on its TS pin (103AT-2 recommended) and holds charging while TS is out of range (SLUSD89B). Without the answer, P2 cannot qualify a charger's temperature input.

questions.question: Is the charger's USB-C input the RP2354B's USB port, or a USB-C connector of its own?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:370 states it is not stated. On a port shared with the RP2354B's USB device, a Default advertisement makes the board follow the USB 2.0 specification as a device. A Sink with no USB data function attaches as a Power Sinking Device and may draw up to 500 mA (USB Type-C Release 2.5, section 4.6.2.1). A charger that runs BC 1.2 detection on D+ and D- would also sit on the RP2354B's data lines. Without the answer, P2 cannot qualify the charger's input detection or the CC detector.

questions.question: Does the pack's protection sit in the pack, as a part off the board bought at Digi-Key (rule 1), or on the IO board, as an LCSC part that JLCPCB places?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:360 puts the protection 'on the 2S pack' without saying where it is mounted. The pack reaches the board by its power and balance leads (IOBoard.md:365, :506), so the cells are off the board. Rule 1 routes a part by where it sits. P2 takes the LCSC number, the vendor and the placements per board from that.

questions.question: Besides overcurrent, which protections must the pack's protection carry: per-cell overvoltage on charge (threshold in V), short circuit (threshold in A), over-temperature (threshold in °C), or none?
questions.why: Research.md:27 has R7 select 'the pack's protection', and IOBoard.md:360 specifies only overcurrent. The 3.0 V per-cell floor is R5's disconnect (IOBoard.md:327). Protection ICs for 2S packs differ in which of these functions they carry. P2 cannot qualify one without the list.

questions.question: Rule 1 has the 18650 cells, a part off the board, bought at Digi-Key, and Digi-Key's API returned no cell from an S9 maker on 2026-09-28. Which vendor sells the cells and counts them for rules 4 and 5?
questions.why: Digi-Key product lookups returned HTTP 404 for INR18650-30Q, INR18650-P28A, NCR18650B, INR18650-35E, INR18650MJ1, US18650VTC6 and INR18650-25P (api.digikey.com/products/v4, 2026-09-28T10:28:20Z to 10:28:28Z). Keyword searches for 'Samsung SDI 18650', 'Molicel 18650', 'Panasonic NCR18650', 'Murata 18650 US18650' and 'LG 18650 INR18650' returned no product (10:27:58Z to 10:28:07Z). '18650 rechargeable lithium ion cell' returned 78 results (50 read, 10:30:58Z), all from ENEPAQ, Dantona Industries and PKCELL. The jlcparts copy of 2026-09-14 holds no 18650 cell row from an S9 maker (queried 2026-09-28T10:32:48Z). These searches do not prove Digi-Key carries none. Without a vendor that stocks an allowed cell, P2 cannot pass a cell through rules 1, 4 and 5.

questions.question: With USB-C present, no DC input, and the pack flat or opened by the 3.0 V floor disconnect, does the IO board run from USB-C? If yes, up to what current, in A at 5 V, does the power path deliver to the board?
questions.why: The owner decision at Research.md:61 names only the DC input and the pack as the board's sources. F8 (Research.md:536) makes USB-C the charge source. IOBoard.md:384 says it is not stated whether USB powers the logic when neither source is present. Power.md:91 says an NVDC (narrow voltage direct current) power path lets the bench start from a flat pack. The BQ25887 has no power path (SLUSD89B Section 5, read 2026-09-28T10:36:56Z). Without the answer, P2 cannot choose between a charger that feeds the board from VBUS and a load-sharing path beside the charger. It also cannot size the current that path carries.

questions.question: Must the charger charge the pack while R5's 3.0 V floor disconnect is open, with the charger connected on the cells' side of the disconnect? Answer yes or no.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:330 says the condition that reconnects the pack after a disconnect is not stated. F9's proposed answer, 'Reconnection only when the DC input or the charger is present', is not an answer (Research.md:501). A charger behind the disconnect cannot charge a pack the floor has opened until the pack reconnects. Without the answer, P2 cannot place the charger's battery terminal and the pack's protection relative to the disconnect, or qualify the power path.

questions.question: The motor monitor (INA238) and the ESC's telemetry (extended DShot at 0.25 V and 1 A a count, or OpenYGE) can both report. Which source then fills the BENCH page's voltage and current registers (page 0x20, registers 0 and 1)? Answer with a rule, for example: the monitor whenever it answers, and the telemetry only when no monitor answers.
questions.why: The page makes it a P1 ask (Research.md:286). It decides whether the INA238's reading is the bench's reading of record. That sets the accuracy the monitor and both shunts are qualified against. The page has one register for each quantity (link_pages.h:230-231).
questions.for_quantity: BENCH voltage and current register source
questions.asks: BENCH voltage and current register source

questions.question: At what motor current, in A, does the coprocessor's overcurrent action trip? Give a figure for the onboard path (150 A continuous, F2) and one for the external path.
questions.why: The INA238 must read up to the threshold inside ±40.96 mV. That caps the onboard shunt at 40.96 mV divided by the threshold (273 µΩ at 150 A, 205 µΩ at 200 A), and the external shunt the same way. P5 budgets the overcurrent path from it.

questions.question: At what temperature, in °C, does the over-temperature action trip?
questions.why: The sensor that feeds the action must cover and resolve that temperature. P2 cannot set that sensor's range or accuracy requirement without it.

questions.question: Which temperature does the over-temperature action watch? The candidates are the sensor beside the onboard shunt, the motor's infrared or thermocouple channel (F5), the ESC's telemetry temperature, the INA238's die temperature, or more than one of them.
questions.why: It decides whether the onboard shunt's sensor feeds a safety action, which sets its accuracy and read path. It also decides whether the over-temperature threshold applies to an R8 part or an R12 part.

questions.question: How long, in ms, must the motor current stay above the overcurrent threshold before the action trips? Or is one conversion above it enough?
questions.why: It sets the INA238's conversion time and averaging (50 µs to 4.12 ms, 1 to 1024 samples, SLYS025B) and its alert behaviour. It is also the first term of P5's budget for the overcurrent path.

questions.question: What is the longest time, in ms, from overcurrent detection to the ESC pack switch open?
questions.why: P5's budget of the motor overcurrent path (Research.md:359) checks this sum against it: the INA238's conversion and alert, the poll or ALERT read, the coprocessor's action and the switch's turn-off. Without it the INA238's alert path cannot be qualified.
questions.for_quantity: Longest time from detection to the ESC pack switch open
questions.asks: longest time from detection to the ESC pack switch open

questions.question: What opens the ESC pack switch on a motor overcurrent? The options are the coprocessor's firmware, the INA238's ALERT output wired to the switch driver, or nothing (the action disarms the outputs and the switch follows the enable node only). The Not defeatable rule (IOBoard.md:197) allows no processor, register or firmware in the path from GPIO6 to either gate, and the coprocessor cannot remove the enable.
questions.why: Research.md:359 budgets the path to the switch's turn-off, but the switch follows the enable node alone. P2 cannot tell whether the INA238's ALERT must drive a switch input. That input would set the ALERT's polarity, level and timing requirements.
questions.for_quantity: Element that opens the ESC pack switch on a motor overcurrent

questions.question: The INA238 has no charge or energy register (datasheet SLYS025B, Table 6-3); the INA228 has both. Are the BENCH charge (mAh) and energy (0.1 Wh) integrated in firmware from the INA238's current and power readings, and if so at what sample period in ms? Or must the motor monitor accumulate them in hardware?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:417 requires the monitor's own accumulators, and the fixed INA238 has none. P2 cannot qualify the motor monitor against that line until the owner states which holds.

questions.question: What resistance range must the external shunt have, in µΩ? The pages give busbar type, 50 to 100 µΩ, from Power.md's table at 300 A, with no owner date. 100 µΩ reaches the INA238's ±40.96 mV at 409.6 A.
questions.why: P2 selects the external shunt within this range. The range was never decided, and its upper end depends on the external path's highest current.

questions.question: What is the highest current, in A, the external shunt path must carry and measure? The owner's answer gives 'above 150 A to 300 A and more'.
questions.why: The external shunt's resistance must keep that current inside ±40.96 mV, and its power rating follows from it. At 300 A the class dissipates 4.5 to 9 W; at 500 A, 12.5 W on 50 µΩ, and 100 µΩ is out of range.

questions.question: Is the external path's highest current continuous or a peak? If a peak, for how long, in s?
questions.why: F2 answers this for the onboard path only. The external shunt's power rating and temperature rise follow from it: 9 W continuous at 300 A on 100 µΩ needs a different part from a 10 s peak.

questions.question: What resolution must the motor current reading have on the external path, in mA? Power.md states that 25 mA (50 µΩ) is below the noise of a running ESC. That noise is not measured.
questions.why: It chooses between 50 µΩ (25 mA, 4.5 W at 300 A) and 100 µΩ (12.5 mA, 9 W). Without it P2 has no figure to rank the external shunt against.
questions.for_quantity: Motor current resolution needed on the external path

questions.question: What accuracy must the motor current reading hold, in % of reading plus an offset in A, on the onboard path and on the external path?
questions.why: The shunt's tolerance and temperature coefficient are qualified against it, and so are the INA238's gain error (±0.1 %) and offset (±5 µV, 50 mA on 100 µΩ). Neither page states it (IOBoard.md:476).

questions.question: What accuracy must the pack voltage reading hold up to 67.2 V, in mV or % of reading?
questions.why: The INA238's bus input has ±0.1 % gain error and ±5 mV offset (SLYS025B), and any divider or filter adds to it. P2 cannot qualify the bus-voltage path without a figure (IOBoard.md:476).

questions.question: Over which ambient temperature range, in °C, must the current and voltage readings hold their accuracy? The monostable's window is specified over 0 to 50 °C (pull request #167). No range is stated for the measurement.
questions.why: Shunt temperature coefficients (ppm/°C) and monitor drift (INA238 gain ±25 ppm/°C) are qualified over a range. Without it the accuracy figures cannot be checked.
questions.for_quantity: Ambient range the measurement accuracy holds over

questions.question: What is the highest power, in W, the onboard shunt may dissipate at 150 A continuous? A 100 µΩ shunt dissipates 2.25 W and a 200 µΩ shunt 4.5 W.
questions.why: With the resolution and the overcurrent threshold, it fixes the onboard shunt's resistance and power rating. The tree gives the two examples and no limit.

questions.question: What range, in °C, and what accuracy, in °C, must the temperature sensor beside the onboard shunt have?
questions.why: P2 qualifies the sensor against them (seeds TMP117 and TMP1075). The tree states only that a sensor sits beside the shunt (IOBoard.md:422).
questions.for_quantity: Onboard shunt temperature sensor range and accuracy

questions.question: What is the highest voltage, in V, a port current monitor must measure and withstand at its inputs? Power.md labels the port monitors '≤15 V' with no source. The ports cut off above 6.0 V or 8.7 V (F16).
questions.why: A replacement for the INA3221 is qualified on its common-mode and bus-voltage rating. The only figure in the pages has no source.

questions.question: What is the highest current, in A, a port current monitor channel must read? The servo procedures act on 3.0 A a servo and 4.0 A a pair. The rail stops at 6.35 A.
questions.why: It sets the full scale a port monitor needs, and the port shunt's value and power rating. A held part such as the 2.5 A Hall sensor passes or fails on it (IOBoard.md:380).

questions.question: What is the longest time, in ms, from a port's current exceeding the 3.0 A ceiling to the abort?
questions.why: It sets the conversion time and the read of 20 channels a port monitor must meet. The INA3221 takes 140 µs to 8.244 ms a conversion, with up to 6 conversions a cycle. The tree says only 'at once' (docs/Servo.md:35) and states no sample rate (IOBoard.md:380).

questions.question: What accuracy and noise, in mA, must a port current reading hold? The host model assumes 0.02 A peak-to-peak noise, and the servo procedures act on differences of 0.08 A and 0.15 A.
questions.why: P2 qualifies a port monitor and its shunt on offset, gain error and noise against it. The only figure is a modelling assumption.

questions.question: Must the 3.0 A servo abort be carried by a hardware alert output of the port monitor? Or is the firmware check at every sample enough?
questions.why: A replacement for the INA3221 passes or fails on whether it has a per-channel limit and an alert pin, and P5 counts alert pins as GPIO. The page states the alert with no decision behind it.

questions.question: Does the servo rail keep a current monitor of its own beside the 20 port monitors? docs/Manifest.md lists the INA745A on the servo rail as selected.
questions.why: P2 selects a servo rail monitor only if one is required. The owner decision names only the per-port channels.

questions.question: Does each motor shunt sit in the ESC pack's positive lead (high side) or in its return (low side)? Answer for the onboard path and for the external path. On the high side the sense leads sit at up to 67.2 V to ground; on the low side they sit within the shunt drop of ground.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:469 states it as not known and names R8. It sets the common-mode voltage at the INA238's IN+ and IN− (−0.3 to 85 V, SLYS025B section 5.3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina238.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z). It also decides whether the external sense leads carry pack voltage onto the IO board's connector, which sets the voltage rating and protection of the sense input. A low-side shunt puts its drop, 15 mV at 150 A on 100 µΩ, between the ESC's return and the star ground (IOBoard.md:547).
questions.for_quantity: Shunt position in the ESC pack path

questions.question: When a test runs through the external path, where does that path's INA238 take the pack voltage for its VBUS input? The options are a separate voltage-sense lead from the pack, the external shunt's pack-side sense lead, or no connection, with no voltage reading on the external path.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:470 states it as not known and names R8. The two paths replace each other, and only the sense leads reach the board (IOBoard.md:403-406). The page measures voltage at the pack (docs/Screens.md:131-132), and the BENCH voltage and power registers depend on it (link_pages.h:230-232). The answer decides whether the external input carries a lead at up to 67.2 V (F15). The INA238's VBUS input takes 0 to 85 V at 0.8 to 1.2 MΩ (SLYS025B 5.5, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z).

questions.question: What is the highest voltage, in V, the external sense input must withstand without damage, between its two sense leads and from either lead to the board's ground? The fault cases include a sense lead on the wrong terminal, a lead off, and the load side shorted to ground.
questions.why: The INA238 is rated at ±40 V between IN+ and IN− and at −0.3 to 85 V on either input (SLYS025B section 5.1, read 2026-09-28T10:35:12Z). Its section 7.1.4 names a short on the load side of the shunt as a case that puts the full supply voltage across the shunt. The pack reaches 67.2 V (F15), above the ±40 V limit, and the operator cables the external path for each test (IOBoard.md:405-406). Without a figure, the input in front of the fixed INA238 cannot be qualified. It may need series resistance and clamps.
questions.for_quantity: External sense input fault withstand voltage

questions.question: Must a port current monitor channel read current that flows back into the servo rail, from a back-driven or braking servo? If so, down to how many A in that direction? Or is a range from 0 A to the positive full scale enough?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:477 states that whether a negative current is measured is not stated. The held ACS70331EESATR-2P5U3 reads 0 to 2.5 A only (ACS70331-DS Rev. 9 selection guide, https://www.allegromicro.com/-/media/files/datasheets/acs70331-datasheet.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:37:10Z). The INA3221 reads −163.84 to 163.8 mV (SBOS576C 6.5, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina3221.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:35:13Z). A unidirectional replacement passes or fails on the answer.
questions.for_quantity: Negative current on a port channel

questions.question: What is the lowest cell count, in cells, of an ESC pack that the cell monitor reads on its balance lead? The page gives 1 to 16 cells. F15 gives only the top, 16 cells. The 1 is the lower bound of SET_PACK_CELLS, which the settings table sets as a physical limit ('a pack cannot have zero cells').
questions.why: P2 cannot keep or drop a monitor by its lowest cell count. BQ76952 reads 3 to 16 cells and BQ76942 3 to 10 (ti.com, read 2026-09-28T10:26Z). A monitor that takes its supply from the stack needs a stack voltage that a 1-cell or 2-cell pack may not reach.
questions.for_quantity: lowest cell count of the ESC pack on the balance lead

questions.question: What resolution, in mV, does each cell voltage reading need? The screen prints each cell to 0.01 V, the pack mean to 0.001 V and the spread in whole mV. The per-cell resistance under load divides a cell's voltage change by the current change, so this resolution also bounds the resistance.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the resolution per cell as not stated (R9). Without it P2 cannot drop a monitor whose converter is too coarse.

questions.question: What largest error, in mV, may each cell voltage reading have under load, and over which ambient temperature range, in °C? The spread verdict switches at 30 mV and 60 mV between two cells (shared/ui/battery_screen.c:46-47).
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the accuracy per cell as not stated (R9). The tree states the board's ambient range only for the monostable's window, 0 to 50 °C (IOBoard.md:184). P2 cannot check a datasheet's total measurement error without the figure and its temperature range.

questions.question: What is the lowest cell voltage, in V, that the cell monitor reads within that error? F15 sets the top at 4.2 V a cell. The ESC pack's chemistry and discharge floor are not stated.
questions.why: A datasheet states its cell error over a limited input range. P2 cannot check that range against the cells the bench reads.

questions.question: How often, in ms, does the cell monitor read every cell of a 16-cell pack? The coprocessor samples the bench numbers every 20 ms (IOBoard.md:431). No rate is stated for the cells.
questions.why: P2 cannot check a monitor's conversion time for 16 cells, or its bus traffic, against a rate that is not stated.

questions.question: What largest time, in µs, may separate the first and the last cell sample of one reading of the pack? The spread is measured under load (IOBoard.md:437), where each cell's voltage follows the ESC's current.
questions.why: A monitor that converts the cells one after another over milliseconds reads each cell at a different current, and shows a spread the pack does not have. P2 cannot choose between simultaneous and sequential conversion without this figure.

questions.question: What largest time, in µs, may separate a cell voltage sample from the motor current sample it is paired with for the per-cell resistance under load? The current comes from the INA238 (R8).
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists how the cell samples align with the current as not stated (R9). P2 cannot qualify a monitor's trigger or timestamp against the INA238's conversion without it.

questions.question: What voltage, in V, must the cell monitor's balance-lead input be rated for, above the 67.2 V of F15? Round 2 selects the overvoltage protection on the balance-lead connector (Research.md:28), which clamps under that rating. No line places the balance lead behind R3's input protection on the ESC pack's power path.
questions.why: P2 cannot drop a monitor whose absolute maximum sits too close to 67.2 V for a clamp to fit under it. P5's ESC pack node clamp check needs the figure.

questions.question: What largest voltage, in V, may stand between the ESC pack's negative at the balance lead and the IO board's ground during a motor test? If the cell monitor is isolated from the RP2354B instead, what isolation voltage, in V? The ESC pack's return reaches the star point by its own lead (testbench/WIRING.md:37-39). Which side of the motor supply the shunts sit on is not stated (IOBoard.md:469). The isolation between the 150 A path and the 3.3 V I²C bus is not defined (IOBoard.md:497).
questions.why: Without the offset or the isolation voltage, P2 cannot choose between a monitor on the board's ground, read directly over I²C or SPI, and one behind an isolated interface, or qualify either.

questions.question: What largest current, in µA, may the cell monitor draw from any one pin of the ESC pack's balance lead, with the IO board powered and with it unpowered? An uneven draw across the pins discharges the cells unevenly and opens the spread the screen judges.
questions.why: A monitor that takes its supply from the top of the stack draws from the upper pins. P2 cannot qualify a monitor's supply and input currents without a limit.

questions.question: What voltages, in V, must the balance-lead input survive from a mis-plugged lead: the largest reverse voltage on any pin against the lead's lowest pin, and the largest voltage between two adjacent pins? A lead plugged in reversed, or shifted by one pin, puts these voltages on the input.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the protection against a mis-plugged lead as not stated (R9). P2 cannot check a monitor's absolute maximum ratings on its cell inputs against mis-plug cases that are not stated.

questions.question: How many connectors, of how many cells each, carry the ESC pack's balance lead to the IO board? A 16-cell pack's balance lead can arrive as one lead or as several. A lead plugged in without the others leaves inputs open.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:485 lists the balance-lead connector sizes as not stated (R9). Round 2 selects the connector part (Research.md:28). Without the arrangement, P2 cannot check which inputs a monitor sees open, or whether it survives the leads plugged in any order.

questions.question: May a jumper or an adapter lead set the cell count at the balance-lead input? Answer yes or no, and if yes, the number of positions. With no setting, a pack of any count from the lowest to 16 cells plugs in with no change on the board.
questions.why: Some monitors need unused cell inputs shorted, or take their supply from the top cell. They read a smaller pack only through such a setting. P2 cannot keep or drop them without the answer.

questions.question: What resolution, in mΩ, does each cell's resistance under load need, and over what smallest step of the motor current, in A, is it taken? The battery screen carries one resistance per cell in mΩ (shared/ui/include/battery_screen.h:16). It prints the pack's sum to 0.1 mΩ (shared/ui/battery_screen.c:295). No line states a figure for the resistance.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:436 requires the per-cell resistance under load and gives no figure. A cell of R mΩ moves by R × I mV over a current step of I A. The cell voltage resolution and error that the resistance needs follow only from both figures. P2 cannot check a monitor's resolution and error against the resistance without them.

questions.question: Does the cell monitor find the plugged pack's cell count, and whether any pack is plugged in, from the balance lead itself, or does the count come from the Cells setting, SET_PACK_CELLS? Answer 'from the lead' or 'from the setting'. The battery screen shows NO PACK, 'nothing on the lead', when its state is not valid (shared/ui/battery_screen.c:233; shared/ui/include/battery_screen.h:27). Its state carries the cell count (battery_screen.h:14). No line states where the count comes from.
questions.why: Finding the count from the lead needs a monitor that detects an open or absent input on each of its 16 cell inputs. With the count from the setting, a pack whose count differs from the setting leaves inputs open or cells unread. P2 cannot keep or drop a monitor by its open-input detection without the answer.

questions.question: What is the highest motor speed, in rpm, at which the vibration path must resolve the once-per-revolution fundamental?
questions.why: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:448 takes 167 Hz at 10,000 rpm from docs/Balance.md:60-62, and IOBoard.md:487 calls 10,000 rpm an example. The fundamental is rpm / 60 Hz: 167 Hz at 10,000 rpm and 1,092 Hz at the BENCH register's ceiling of 65,535 rpm. Without the bound, P2 cannot set the converter's lowest sample rate or drop a candidate on it.
questions.for_quantity: highest motor speed the vibration path resolves

questions.question: What sample rate, in samples per second, must the converter reach on each vibration channel?
questions.why: Not stated (hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:493). Resolving the fundamental alone takes more than 2 × rpm / 60 samples a second, which is 333 S/s at 10,000 rpm. The blade-pass frequency is blades × rpm / 60. At 6 blades (docs/Balance.md:19 takes 2 to 6) and 10,000 rpm it is 1,000 Hz, and it aliases into the measured band unless it is filtered out or sampled. The candidates' rates span three orders of magnitude. ADS1115: 8 to 860 S/s (SBAS444E, read 2026-09-28T10:30:15Z, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1115.pdf). ADS112C04: up to 2,000 S/s (SBAS894A, read 2026-09-28T10:30:16Z, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads112c04.pdf). ADS131M04: up to 64,000 S/s (SBAS890D, read 2026-09-28T10:30:16Z, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads131m04.pdf). RP2354B's ADC: 500,000 S/s (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 12.4, read 2026-09-28T10:24:43Z, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf). Without this figure, P2 cannot drop a converter on its rate.

questions.question: What is the smallest vibration amplitude at the fundamental, in mg (thousandths of standard gravity), that the balance measurement must resolve?
questions.why: Neither page states the resolution the balance measurement needs. Q4 has R10 report each alternative's ENOB against the balance measurement (hardware/docs/Research.md:572), and P2 drops a converter that misses it. Together with the full scale in the next question, it sets the dynamic range the converter needs. The RP2354B's ADC gives 9.2 ENOB in section 12.4 and 9 bits minimum, 9.5 typical in Table 1438 of the RP2350 datasheet, build 2025-07-29 (read 2026-09-28T10:24:43Z).

questions.question: What is the largest vibration amplitude, in g, that the vibration path must take without clipping?
questions.why: Not stated. The accelerometer is not chosen (hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:493), and R11 selects it in T4 at the same time as R10. With the smallest amplitude to resolve, this value fixes the converter's dynamic range, so without it P2 cannot state the ENOB a candidate needs.

questions.question: What input voltage span, in volts, must the converter take at its accelerometer input?
questions.why: The accelerometer's output range is not stated (hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:493). R11 selects the accelerometer in the same task as R10, so neither category can take the other's range as given. The RP2354B's ADC takes 0 V to ADC_AVDD (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Table 1438) and no more than IOVDD (section 12.4, read 2026-09-28T10:24:43Z). IOVDD is the 3.3 V rail, held within ±3 % at the monostable (hardware/docs/Research.md:283). The reference supplies ADC_AVDD, so its voltage follows from this span, and an external converter's input range is qualified against it.

questions.question: How many accelerometer axes does the converter sample: 1, or the 2 axes in the firewall's plane?
questions.why: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:451 uses one axis across the shaft. A three-axis part mounted flat on a firewall has two axes in that plane (docs/Balance.md:45-48). How many axes are wired is not stated (IOBoard.md:493). The answer sets the converter's channel count, whether two channels are sampled at one instant, and how many RP2354B ADC inputs P5 counts.

questions.question: What phase error, in degrees at the highest motor speed, may the variation of the delay between a vibration sample and the index pulse add?
questions.why: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:449 counts the variation of the delay, not its constant part (docs/Balance.md:65-67), and states no limit. Q4 has R10 report each alternative's worst-case latency jitter, and whether each conversion can be triggered or timestamped on the index pulse's timebase (hardware/docs/Research.md:572). At 10,000 rpm one revolution takes 6 ms, so 1° is 16.7 µs of timing variation. P2 drops an external converter whose conversion timing misses the limit.

questions.question: What accuracy, in percent of reading, must the vibration amplitude reach?
questions.why: Not stated. The reference sets the gain of the RP2354B's ADC, whose input range is 0 V to ADC_AVDD (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Table 1438, read 2026-09-28T10:24:43Z). P2 needs the figure to qualify a reference's initial accuracy and drift, and an external converter's gain error. The balance correction itself is relative, because the trial run measures the whole chain (docs/Balance.md:65-67), so 'no requirement' is a possible answer. hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:476 names R10 for the accuracy of the pack voltage and the motor current, but the INA238 of R8 measures both (IOBoard.md:415), not R10's converter.

questions.question: Over what ambient temperature range, in °C, must the converter and its reference hold their figures?
questions.why: No page states a board-wide ambient range. The monostable's window and the 3.3 V rail are specified over 0 to 50 °C (hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:184; hardware/docs/Research.md:283), which is that circuit's range only. P2 needs a range to turn a reference's drift in ppm/°C into an error and to check each part's operating range.

questions.question: Does Q4 take a digital accelerometer on SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface), such as the IIS3DWB, as a third alternative beside the RP2354B's ADC with a reference and an external ADC: yes or no?
questions.why: hardware/docs/Research.md:289 (R11, concerns) makes the IIS3DWB a seed 'only if Q4 accepts a digital one'. Q4 (hardware/docs/Research.md:572) names only the two converter alternatives, and tools/research/categories.json gives Q4 only the option classes 'reference' and 'external ADC'. hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:447 takes an analogue sensor from docs/Balance.md:60-63. That passage rules out a fused IMU streaming orientation at 100 Hz, not an accelerometer that streams raw samples faster. No page answers the question. With yes, R10 reports the figures Q4 asks for that alternative too: rate, resolution, and whether each sample can be timestamped on the index pulse's timebase. With no, the IIS3DWB is not a seed.

questions.question: Must the converter for the accelerometer also measure a control surface's static angle from gravity, with an accelerometer on the surface, and if so to what resolution, in degrees?
questions.why: shared/servo/include/servo_sync.h:23-25 and docs/Servo.md:79-80 assign two servos that agree with each other and are both wrong to 'the accelerometer on the surface'. hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:454 repeats this, and shared/ui/stub_screen.c:37-43 says such an accelerometer observes two axes. A static angle is a DC measurement within ±1 g, so the converter's offset and its drift count, and a piezo sensor does not measure it. The balance measurement is AC at the fundamental. The answer therefore changes the input range, the ENOB and the offset figures P2 qualifies a converter against. R11's P1 asks which sensor gives the servo's measured position (Research.md:289). That answer picks the sensor, not whether R10's converter carries it.

questions.question: What is the longest lead, in metres, from the accelerometer on the rig arm or the firewall to the IO board?
questions.why: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:493 lists the lead from the rig arm or firewall to the IO board as not stated, and names Q4 and R10 for the converter. On a complete aircraft the accelerometer sits on the firewall (docs/Balance.md:45), and its lead runs near the motor and ESC wiring. shared/ui/balance_screen.c:476-478 and :499-501 warn that a flapping lead is a second accelerometer. Each RP2354B ADC input takes 0 V to ADC_AVDD on one pin (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, Table 1438, read 2026-09-28T10:35:08Z). The ADS1115, ADS112C04 and ADS131M04 take differential inputs (SBAS444E, SBAS894A and SBAS890D, read 2026-09-28T10:40:52Z to 10:40:54Z from https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/). P2 needs the length to state whether a candidate's input must be differential.

questions.question: Over how many seconds at a steady speed may one balance run average the vibration signal?
questions.why: Q4 compares each alternative's ENOB against the balance measurement (hardware/docs/Research.md:572). The fundamental is extracted over many revolutions, and averaging lowers uncorrelated noise by the square root of the number of samples averaged. The ENOB a converter needs to resolve the smallest amplitude of P1's question 2 therefore depends on how long a run averages. docs/Balance.md:57-69 and shared/ui/balance_screen.c:584-589 give the number of runs, four without an index pulse and half that with one, but no run length. Without the length, P2 cannot set an ENOB threshold, for example for the RP2354B's 9 bits minimum (Table 1438, read 2026-09-28T10:35:08Z).

questions.question: Which sensor gives the servo's measured position that the servo screen draws beside the commanded one? The choices are: the F4 encoder mounted on the servo output shaft; a sensor of its own that R11 selects (for example a magnetic angle sensor at the horn); or none in round 1.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:454 specifies no input and names the F4 encoder only as one that can sit on the servo output shaft. Until the sensor is named, P2 cannot tell whether this function needs a part, or which one. The screen takes the position as a pulse width in µs (shared/ui/include/servo_screen.h:67).

questions.question: If a sensor other than the F4 encoder gives the servo's measured position: what angular resolution must it have, in degrees, over what horn travel, in degrees?
questions.why: The tree gives no resolution or range for the measured position. The commanded side has 1 µs steps over 500 to 2500 µs (IOBoard.md:50), which fixes no angle. P2 cannot qualify an angle sensor without these. Not needed if the answer is the F4 encoder.

questions.question: When more than one rotation input reports (optical index, magnetic pickup, phase-wire clip, encoder, ESC telemetry), which one fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action? The choices are: a fixed priority order (state the order), or the one input a panel setting picks.
questions.why: The BENCH page has one rpm register with one valid bit (shared/link/include/link_pages.h:233; IOBoard.md:432). The stall action's rpm source is not stated either (IOBoard.md:434). Without the answer, P2 cannot say which inputs must run at the same time, or at what update rate.

questions.question: What is the highest shaft speed, in rpm, that the rotation inputs and the vibration path must follow?
questions.why: It sets each front end's highest input frequency. For the optical index, the encoder's index and the vibration fundamental that is rpm / 60. For the phase-wire clip, and for a pickup that reads the rotor's magnets, it is rpm / 60 × pole pairs, up to 21 pairs (MOTOR_POLES up to 42, docs/Link.md:159-160). 10,000 rpm is only Balance.md's example (docs/Balance.md:60-62). The BENCH register stops at 65,535 rpm.
questions.for_quantity: highest rpm the rotation inputs and the vibration path follow

questions.question: Down to which shaft speed, in rpm, must at least one rotation input keep reading, including the coast-down after a disarm?
questions.why: The ESC's speed stops 200 ms after the disarm (firmware/iomcu/src/outputs_hw.c:294-295; firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:663), so another input has to cover the coast-down (IOBoard.md:489). A phase-wire clip then reads back-EMF, and a variable-reluctance pickup's output, both of which fall with speed. Without the lowest speed, P2 cannot set those front ends' sensitivity or say which input covers the coast-down.
questions.for_quantity: lowest rpm the rotation inputs read

questions.question: What peak voltage, in V, must the phase-wire clip's input withstand: the 67.2 V of F15 plus what margin for switching overshoot and ringing on the motor phase?
questions.why: F15 (Research.md:543) bounds the pack, not the phase node, which rings above the pack at each switching edge. IOBoard.md:443 rates the clip at 67.2 V with no margin. The ESC pack switch's 67.2 V rating takes a margin that is asked for (IOBoard.md:189). Without the peak, P2 cannot qualify the clip's divider, clamp and comparator input.

questions.question: How does the phase-wire clip couple to the motor phase: galvanically, clipped onto the bare conductor, or without contact, through the wire's insulation?
questions.why: A galvanic clip needs a high-voltage divider and a clamp; a non-contact clip needs a high-impedance amplifier. The clip's conditioning is not stated (IOBoard.md:491). P2 cannot choose the front end's topology or qualify its parts without it.

questions.question: Is the phase-wire input galvanically isolated from the 3.3 V logic, and if so, to what isolation voltage, in V? Or is it referenced to the ground that the ESC pack's return shares at the star point?
questions.why: The isolation is not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The ESC pack's return reaches the star point by its own lead (IOBoard.md:547), so a divider referenced to that ground is possible. An isolator or an isolated supply would be a part R11 selects. Without the answer, P2 cannot tell whether that part is needed or qualify it.
questions.for_quantity: phase-wire clip isolation from the 3.3 V logic

questions.question: Which magnetic pickup does the input take, and does R11 select it or does the operator bring it? The choices are: a Hall-effect sensor with a digital output (state its supply voltage, in V), or a variable-reluctance coil with an AC output (state its peak voltage, in V).
questions.why: The pickup's type, supply and output are not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The owner's decision names only a magnetic rpm pickup (Research.md:65). A Hall sensor needs a supply, a pull-up and translation to 3.3 V; a coil needs a comparator with hysteresis and a clamp. P2 cannot choose between these front ends.
questions.for_quantity: magnetic pickup type, supply and output

questions.question: How many pulses per revolution does the magnetic pickup give: one per magnet added to the bell (state how many magnets), or one per rotor pole pair (MOTOR_POLES / 2, up to 21)?
questions.why: Whether the pickup's reading uses MOTOR_POLES is not stated (IOBoard.md:490). The highest rpm times this count sets the front end's highest input frequency, which P2 qualifies the front end against.

questions.question: Does R11 select the optical index sensor itself (a reflective sensor on a lead, aimed from below at the pen line on the motor bell), or only the IO board's front end for a sensor the operator brings? In the second case, at what supply voltage, in V, and with which output: open collector, push-pull or analogue?
questions.why: The optical index sensor's type, supply and output are not stated (IOBoard.md:491). The seeds for it, TLV3201 and TLV7011, are comparators only (Research.md:289). P2 cannot tell which parts this function takes.
questions.for_quantity: optical index sensor type, supply and output

questions.question: If R11 selects the optical index sensor: at what distance, in mm, does it read the pen line on the motor bell?
questions.why: A reflective sensor is specified for a working distance. The tree gives the mark and where it goes (docs/Balance.md:32-37) but no distance. P2 cannot qualify a sensor head without it.

questions.question: The accelerometer sits on the rig arm or the firewall. How is it built and bought: on a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles (parts with LCSC numbers, under the IO board's sourcing rules), or as a part or module off the board, bought at Digi-Key (sourcing rule 1)?
questions.why: The accelerometer sits away from the IO board (docs/Balance.md:38-39, :45-46; IOBoard.md:493). Sourcing rule 1 (Research.md:134-139) covers a part on the IO board and a part off it, not a second assembled board. Without the answer, P2 cannot tell whether to search jlcparts or Digi-Key, or which stock gate applies.

questions.question: How long is the lead from the accelerometer on the rig arm or the firewall to the IO board, in m?
questions.why: The lead is not stated (IOBoard.md:493). Its capacitance loads the sensor's analogue output, and its length sets the noise it picks up. Together they decide whether the sensor end needs a buffer or a differential driver. P2 cannot qualify the output drive without the length.

questions.question: What full-scale acceleration, in g, must the vibration sensor measure without clipping?
questions.why: The tree states no range. P2 cannot qualify a sensor's measurement range without one.

questions.question: What is the smallest vibration amplitude at the rotation fundamental, in mg, that the balance measurement must resolve?
questions.why: It sets the sensor's allowed noise over the measurement bandwidth and, with the full scale, the dynamic range. The tree does not state it. P2 cannot qualify a sensor's noise density without it.

questions.question: What phase error, in degrees at the highest rpm, may delay variation add across the whole vibration chain: the accelerometer, the index pulse's front end and the converter together?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:449 says a constant delay cancels and its variation counts, but gives no limit. P2 cannot qualify the accelerometer's phase response or the index comparator's delay spread without a stated budget. R10 reports the converter's latency jitter for Q4 against the same figure.

questions.question: May the vibration sensor be a digital accelerometer with raw, unfused output and a known sampling instant (the IIS3DWB class, on SPI), or must it be analogue?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:447 requires an analogue sensor on the strength of docs/Balance.md:57-63. That page rules out a fused IMU streaming at 100 Hz, not a raw digital accelerometer. Research.md:289 makes the IIS3DWB a seed only if Q4 accepts a digital sensor. Q4 (Research.md:572) offers two analogue converters only and is decided after the research, so no digital part is ever qualified for it. Without the answer, P2 cannot set R11's candidate list.

questions.question: Are the encoder's 1 MHz (single-ended) and 5 MHz (RS-422) figures the count rate, in counts per second over A and B together, or the frequency of each of A and B, in Hz (a quarter of the count rate)?
questions.why: F4 asked for the highest count rate, and the answer gives MHz (Research.md:532). If 5 MHz is the frequency of each channel, the count rate is 20 million counts per second, four times the other reading. P2 cannot qualify the receivers, or R11 report the decode (IOBoard.md:446), without the unit.

questions.question: With the supply jumper at 12 V and the single-ended form selected, what is the highest signal voltage, in V, the single-ended input takes: 5 V, or the 12 V of an encoder whose push-pull outputs swing to its supply (HTL, high-threshold logic)?
questions.why: F4 sets the single-ended form at 5 V, and a separate jumper sets the supply to 5 V or 12 V (Research.md:532). An encoder on 12 V can output 12 V. P2 cannot qualify the input's voltage rating, or its translation to 3.3 V (IOBoard.md:105), without it.

questions.question: What range of ESC PWM (pulse-width modulation) switching frequency, in kHz, must the phase-wire clip's front end reject while it passes the motor's electrical frequency? The programmer screen offers 24, 48 and 96 kHz (shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:115). Does that range apply, or a wider one?
questions.why: The phase node carries the ESC's PWM chopping on top of the commutation. The electrical frequency is rpm / 60 × pole pairs. At the BENCH register's 65,535 rpm with 21 pole pairs (docs/Link.md:159-160) that is 22.9 kHz, next to a 24 kHz PWM. The clip's conditioning is not stated (IOBoard.md:491), and no switching frequency to reject is given. Without it P2 cannot qualify the comparator's speed and hysteresis, or choose between a filtered comparator and another topology.
questions.for_quantity: phase-wire clip PWM switching frequency rejected

questions.question: What is the lowest shaft speed, in rpm, at which a balance run is measured?
questions.why: It sets the lowest vibration fundamental, rpm / 60, that the sensor must pass. The specification allows a piezo sensor (IOBoard.md:447), which is AC-coupled and has a low-frequency corner that must sit below that fundamental. P1's lowest-speed question covers the rotation inputs and the coast-down, not the vibration path. IOBoard.md:448 gives only the 167 Hz example at 10,000 rpm. Without it P2 cannot qualify a piezo sensor's low-frequency response.

questions.question: Across what ambient temperature range, in °C, must the sensors mounted at the motor work? That is the accelerometer on the rig arm or firewall, and the optical and magnetic sensors if R11 selects them.
questions.why: The tree states no operating temperature for a part off the IO board. The only range in the specification is 0 to 50 °C, for the monostable window (IOBoard.md:184, :220). The accelerometer goes hard against the motor (docs/Balance.md:38-39; shared/ui/balance_screen.c:212-215), beside a motor whose temperature the bench measures (F5). P2 cannot check a sensor's rated temperature range against nothing.
questions.for_quantity: operating temperature at the sensor mount

questions.question: Which motor temperature channel, infrared or thermocouple, fills the BENCH page's one motor temperature register (register 5, 0.1 °C signed, valid bit 4)? Or does a second register carry the other channel?
questions.why: The BENCH page has one motor temperature register and one valid bit (shared/link/include/link_pages.h:235, :269), and F5 fixes 2 channels (IOBoard.md:458, :483). Without the answer P2 cannot state which channel's reading the register's 0.1 °C signed format and the 20 ms bench sampling apply to. Nor can it state whether the other channel feeds a register that does not exist yet.

questions.question: Which thermocouple type (a letter, such as K, J or T) does the thermocouple channel take?
questions.why: F5 names a thermocouple and no type (Research.md:533). P2 checks each front end's supported types and linearisation, and the type sets the range question 2 applies.

questions.question: What motor temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the thermocouple channel measure?
questions.why: Neither page states a range. The register's -3,276.8 to +3,276.7 °C span (link_pages.h:234-235) bounds nothing. P2 checks each front end's measurement range for the type against it.

questions.question: What accuracy (± °C) must the thermocouple channel give over that range, cold-junction compensation included?
questions.why: Neither page states an accuracy. The register's 0.1 °C step (IOBoard.md:459) is the link's step, not an accuracy. P2 compares each front end's datasheet error, conversion and cold junction together, against it. The cold junction sits at the IO board's connector (IOBoard.md:558). The only ambient range the pages state is the monostable's, 0 to 50 °C (hardware/docs/Monostable.md:27 at 23c82ca).

questions.question: How often (Hz) must the thermocouple channel deliver a new reading?
questions.why: The coprocessor samples the bench numbers every 20 ms (IOBoard.md:431). That is the firmware loop, not a stated need for motor temperature. P2 checks each front end's conversion time, with its filter setting, against it.

questions.question: What voltage (V) must the thermocouple input withstand, without damage, between either lead and the IO board's ground if the junction touches a motor phase or winding?
questions.why: The motor runs from the ESC pack of up to 67.2 V (F15, Research.md:543), and the phase-wire clip is rated for it (IOBoard.md:443). The thermocouple input carries no rating on either page. P2 checks each front end's input absolute maximum or protection against it, or qualifies an isolated input.

questions.question: How long (m) is the lead from the IO board's infrared connector to the infrared sensor at the motor? Answer 0 m if the sensor sits on the IO board.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:558 gives the infrared channel a connector, so the sensor sits off the board. The length decides whether the sensor is a part off the board, bought at Digi-Key with LCSC number none (sourcing rule 1, Research.md:134-139). It also decides which interface the lead carries: a digital sensor's bus capacitance or an analogue signal.

questions.question: What object temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the infrared channel measure?
questions.why: F5 gives an infrared channel and no range (Research.md:533). P2 checks each sensor's object temperature range against it.

questions.question: What accuracy (± °C) must the infrared channel give over that range?
questions.why: Neither page states an accuracy. P2 compares each sensor's datasheet object-temperature accuracy over the range of question 7 against it.

questions.question: What full field of view (degrees) must the infrared sensor have, given its distance to the motor and the surface it must see?
questions.why: An infrared thermometer averages everything inside its field of view, so a view wider than the motor at the mounting distance reads the surroundings. Neither page gives the distance or the surface. P2 selects the sensor's optics variant against it.

questions.question: How often (Hz) must the infrared channel deliver a new reading?
questions.why: The 20 ms bench sampling (IOBoard.md:431) is the firmware loop, not a stated need. P2 checks each sensor's refresh rate against it.

questions.question: At which clock rate (kHz) must the external I2C ports run?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:481 records the coprocessor's I2C bus speed as not stated. The one I2C speed setting, 100 to 400 kHz, belongs to the display's bus (shared/settings/settings.c:105-107, IOBoard.md:597). P2 checks each multiplexer, buffer or extender's rated clock against it (seeds TCA9548A, PCA9615, TCA9617A). The infrared sensor and the store share the coprocessor's buses.

questions.question: What is the longest cable (m) between an external I2C port and the device on it?
questions.why: Q7 fixes 2 Qwiic ports at 3.3 V but no cable length or bus capacitance (Research.md:545). The length decides whether a port needs a buffer or a differential extender, and the capacitance each part must drive.

questions.question: What current (mA) must each external I2C port supply on its 3.3 V pin?
questions.why: A Qwiic port carries its device's 3.3 V supply, and neither page states the current. P2 needs it for a port switch or current limit. R5 sizes the 3.3 V rail from the parts the tasks select, which leaves external devices out (Research.md:283).

questions.question: Which 7-bit I2C addresses (hex) must a device on an external I2C port be free to use?
questions.why: The original requirement puts external current sensors on these ports (docs/Manifest.md:14, :28). The port monitors hold 0x40 to 0x43, and each INA238 0x44 or above, on the RP2354B's 2 I2C buses (IOBoard.md:351, :464). The answer decides whether a port may share a bus with them or needs its own segment behind a multiplexer.

questions.question: What capacity (bytes) must an I2C FRAM or EEPROM store hold for the IO board's output binding?
questions.why: The flash store holds 32 slots of 256 bytes, 8,192 bytes (IOBoard.md:115). Today's record is 148 bytes for 8 slots and 8 channels (firmware/iomcu/src/out_store.c:99-107). The IO board's 20-port record is not defined (IOBoard.md:248). By their part numbers the seeds run from 16 Kbit (FM24CL16B) to 256 Kbit (MB85RC256V, 24LC256). P2 checks each FRAM or EEPROM candidate's capacity against it.

questions.question: How many saves (count) of the output binding must the store survive over the board's life?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:117 gives what the flash store allows: about 3.2 million saves, at 100,000 cycles a sector over 32 slots. Neither page states how many saves the board needs. P2 checks each FRAM or EEPROM candidate's write endurance against it.

questions.question: Where does the infrared motor temperature sensor sit: off the IO board, on a lead to a connector on the IO board, as IOBoard.md:558 assumes, or on the IO board itself?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:558 gives the infrared channel a connector, and no source backs it. F5 (Research.md:533) gives the method and the count only, and Research.md:28 only puts connectors in round 2. The position decides sourcing rule 1: an LCSC number and JLCPCB assembly, or Digi-Key with LCSC number none (Research.md:134-139). It also decides whether the sensor's signal crosses a lead. P1's question 6, the lead's length, rests on this premise.

questions.question: Must the thermocouple channel detect an open or unplugged thermocouple, so that the motor temperature valid bit (BENCH flag bit 4) stays clear while none is fitted? Answer yes or no.
questions.why: IOBoard.md:432 sets each valid bit 'only when a sensor answered' (link_pages.h:246-276). A thermocouple front end answers on its bus whether or not a thermocouple is plugged in. Holding bit 4 clear with no thermocouple needs the front end to report an open input. P2 checks each front end for open-circuit detection against the answer. It applies to the thermocouple channel if question 0 puts it in the register.

questions.question: Over what ambient temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) must the IO board operate, which sets the temperature of the thermocouple's cold junction at its connector?
questions.why: The cold junction sits at the IO board's connector (IOBoard.md:558), so the front end's cold-junction error depends on the board's ambient. IOBoard.md and Research.md state no ambient range. The only one in the sources is the monostable page's 0 to 50 °C, given as 'the range the bench is assumed to be used in' (hardware/docs/Monostable.md:27, :318-319 at 23c82ca). That is an assumption. P2 checks each front end's cold-junction accuracy and operating range against the answer.

questions.question: What ambient temperature range (°C, lowest to highest) does the infrared sensor itself see at its mounting position near the motor?
questions.why: The sensor sits near the motor it measures, so its own temperature is not the IO board's. No source states it. P2 checks each infrared sensor's rated operating range against it, and the object-temperature accuracy its datasheet gives at that ambient.

questions.question: Must a device be plugged into or out of an external I2C port while the board is powered, with the bus and the other devices on it still running? Answer yes or no.
questions.why: Q7 (Research.md:545) fixes the count, level and connector only. A Qwiic lead plugged into a running bus can disturb transfers on the bus it joins, and the port monitors share the coprocessor's buses (IOBoard.md:351, :464). The answer decides whether a port needs a hot-swap buffer or a segment it can reset alone. P2 checks each buffer, multiplexer or extender (seeds TCA9548A, PCA9615, TCA9617A) against it.

questions.question: Which supply gives the 5 V load-cell excitation of F3: the IO board's 5 V rail, which also carries the display's 1.5 A continuous and 2 A peak, or a separate supply for the bridges?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:338 counts the excitation as a load on the 5 V rail. F3 fixes only its voltage. The answer decides three things. First, whether the excitation is the rail itself or a part R13 selects. Second, which analogue supply and reference-input range the bridge ADC must accept. Third, which rail R5 (T3) sizes for the excitation current. P2 cannot qualify the excitation or the ADC's reference input without it.

questions.question: What is the bridge resistance of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in Ω?
questions.why: Each cell draws 5 V divided by its bridge resistance, and the currents of the cells on one excitation add up. IOBoard.md:338 gives the excitation current as not stated. P2 needs the current to rate the excitation part. R5 (T3) needs it to size the 5 V rail. The load cells are not a part T4 selects, so P4 does not report their draw.

questions.question: What is the rated output of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in mV/V?
questions.why: Rated output × 5 V excitation gives each channel's full-scale differential input, in mV. That fixes the input range and programmable gain the bridge ADC needs. Neither page states it.

questions.question: What is the rated capacity of each of the 3 load cells (the thrust cell and the 2 torque cells), in N?
questions.why: It converts a load step in N into a voltage step at the ADC input: step / capacity × rated output × 5 V. Without it, P2 cannot turn the resolution in N into the noise-free resolution in µV a part must reach. Neither page states it.

questions.question: What thrust range, in N, and what torque range, in N·m, must the bench measure, each from its largest negative to its largest positive value?
questions.why: IOBoard.md:495 gives the ranges as not stated and assigns them to R13. They set how much of each cell's full-scale output the ADC input spans. They also set whether each channel reads both signs: reverse thrust, and both directions of rotation.

questions.question: What is the smallest load change, in N, that each load cell's channel must resolve (the thrust cell and each torque cell), at the output rate asked for the load-cell channels?
questions.why: With the rated capacity and the rated output, it gives the step at the ADC input in µV. That is the noise-free resolution the bridge ADC must reach at its data rate. Neither page states a resolution for thrust or torque.

questions.question: What accuracy must each load-cell channel hold, in % of the cell's rated output, counting the bridge ADC's and the excitation's gain and offset errors and their drift with temperature?
questions.why: It bounds the gain error, offset, nonlinearity and drift the ADC may have. It also bounds the excitation's drift if the measurement is not ratiometric. Neither page states an accuracy for thrust or torque.

questions.question: At what output rate must each of the 3 load-cell channels be read, in samples per second per channel?
questions.why: A multiplexed converter splits its data rate across the channels and must settle after each switch. So the rate per channel decides between one multiplexed converter and one converter per channel, and sets the digital filter. The 20 ms sampling at IOBoard.md:431 covers the BENCH numbers, which carry no thrust or torque, so it does not set this rate.

questions.question: How far apart in time, in ms, may the readings of the 2 torque cells, and of the thrust cell, be taken? May one multiplexed converter read them in turn, or must they be converted at the same instant?
questions.why: F3 takes torque from 2 cells. The allowed time between readings decides whether the 3 channels can share one multiplexed converter or need simultaneous conversion. That choice fixes the part and its placements per board, and so the need in the stock gate of sourcing rule 4.

questions.question: Does each load cell connect with 4 wires (excitation and signal) or with 6 wires (excitation, signal and sense leads)?
questions.why: A 6-wire cell's sense leads go to the ADC's reference input. The part then needs a differential reference input for each sensed cell, or the cells share one excitation and one pair of sense leads. P2 cannot count the reference inputs and channels a part needs without this. F3 gives only the channels and the excitation.

questions.question: Over what ambient temperature range, in °C, must each load-cell channel hold the accuracy asked for it?
questions.why: P1's question 6 asks an accuracy that counts drift with temperature. A datasheet gives drift per °C (ppm/°C, nV/°C), so the error it adds depends on the temperature span. The only range in the tree is 0 to 50 °C. It is stated for the monostable window (IOBoard.md:184) and the 3.3 V rail (Research.md:283), not for any measurement. Without the span, P2 cannot turn a part's drift figures into % of rated output.

questions.question: What is the longest time, in ms, from a step change in thrust or torque to a fully settled reading on that channel?
questions.why: A delta-sigma bridge ADC's digital filter delays a step by several conversions. On the ADS1232 and ADS1234 seeds, a fully settled reading after an input step takes 5 readings: 62.5 ms at 80 SPS and 500 ms at 10 SPS (TI SBAS350H, section 7.3.7 and the data-rate table, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads1234.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:36:42Z). The output rate of P1's question 7 does not bound this delay, because parts at the same rate differ in filter order. Neither page states a step response for thrust or torque.
questions.for_quantity: load-cell settling time after a load step

R4: reply path through the gate (the element that passes the bidirectional DShot reply and the half-duplex receive direction while enabled, IOBoard.md:254 and :278)
R5: 2S pack connector (IOBoard.md:373: 'The 2S pack's connector: not stated in the tree. R5, and round 2'; R5 states its current, round 2 selects the part)
